title: Controls menu: keyboard/gamepad diagram with live input highlighting
body:
Replace the plain "KEY - Action" text list in the Flap's Controls tab with a diagram of the keyboard / gamepad, with the mapped keys highlighted.

**Design**: §4 of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-audio-controls-refactor-design.md`
**Tasks**: 1, 9, 10, 11, 12 of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-10-audio-controls-refactor.md`

## Behaviour

- **Device-aware**: shows the keyboard diagram or the gamepad diagram depending on `InputHub.UltimoDeviceFueJoystick`, reacting to `OnDeviceCambio` (same pattern as `SoloConJoystick`).
- **Live input-reactive highlighting**: each hotspot has three states — idle (unmapped), mapped (permanent colour + localized label, this is the "resaltadito"), and pressed (brighter, pulsing) while the control is actually held.
- **Art is swappable**: `ControlsDiagramSettings` (ScriptableObject in `Resources`, self-loading like `TextHighlightSettings`) has one sprite field per device. Valentino drops final art in; no code, no prefab wiring.
- **Placeholder until then**: with an empty sprite field the component draws a procedural placeholder (the `GamepadCursor` / `IconosDeBoton` precedent), so the tab is readable today and the placeholder disappears the moment art is assigned.

## Notes

- The hierarchy is built **by code**, which is this project's established rule for input UI ("everything has to work on Play without touching scenes or prefabs") and avoids blind YAML surgery on `FlapManager.prefab`.
- Hotspot positions are normalized rects in the settings asset. Normalized on purpose: swapping in art at a different resolution keeps them valid — only a different *layout* needs re-tuning. If editing numbers proves annoying, the fallback is an editor tool that spawns draggable hotspot GameObjects (recorded as deferred in the spec).
- `Accion` gets promoted out of `InputPromptSystem` to a top-level enum so both the prompt system and the diagram can name actions. `InputHub` gains read-only held-state properties, which it did not have (gameplay only ever needed edges).
- **B / L1 / R1 / Start / Esc / O also drive Flap navigation**, so their pressed highlight is a blink before the menu reacts. Accepted, not a bug: the diagram only observes input and never consumes it, so it adds no arbitration problem of the #45 / #41.14 family.
- Any pulse animation uses **unscaled** time — the Flap sets `Time.timeScale = 0` exactly when this tab is on screen.
- 8 new `UITexts` keys in es/en/pt for the action labels. `controlsText` stays in the tables, just no longer displayed, so this is reversible.
- Mute (M) is **not** on the diagram: it has no `Accion` member, and widening that enum is a design call, not part of this batch.

Supersedes the remaining concern in #49 (that tab is no longer a text list at all).

title: Dialog: the first field never gets focus, and focus is neither trapped nor returned
body:
Found by an exploratory Playwright run against `ghcr.io/eh-homelab/scadbuddy:main` at `b608a3a`. Three of four testers hit it; one lost a preset to it.

## Steps
Click **Save as preset…**, type a name, then press Enter.

## Actual
- **Focus.** Focus is on the dialog panel (`document.activeElement` is the `div[role=dialog]`), not the name input. Typed text goes nowhere and Enter doesn't submit.
  - One tester's preset was saved as "·Emma – lilac & white", with the first letter lost.
  - Another tester's save silently never happened.
- **Cause.** `components/ui/Dialog.tsx` focuses its panel in an effect on open. That runs after the child input's `autoFocus` and takes focus back.
- **Focus isn't returned.** After Escape, Cancel, a save or a delete, focus goes to `<body>` instead of back to the button that opened the dialog.
- **Focus isn't trapped.** Tab moves out of an `aria-modal="true"` dialog into the page behind it.
- The font picker's "Search fonts" field loses focus the same way.

## Also on the preset row (screen readers)
- "Changed from X" is a plain span, not a live region, so it's never announced.
- **Update** has no context in its accessible name. Delete does: "Delete preset ‹name›".
- The dialog description isn't linked with `aria-describedby`.

## Fix
In `Dialog`:
- On open, focus the first focusable element (or an `[autofocus]` one), falling back to the panel.
- Trap Tab and Shift+Tab inside the dialog.
- On close, restore focus to the element that had it before opening.

This fixes every dialog in the app, not only the preset ones.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Chips have no visible focus indicator (.chip:focus-visible sets outline: 0)
body:
## Summary

`.chip:focus-visible` removes the outline and puts nothing in its place, so a keyboard-focused chip looks exactly like an unfocused one. This affects chips in the chip input, which have `tabindex="0"`, and any chip used as a `<button>` or `<a>`.

## Bootstrap version

`v6-dev` @ [`3df38af`](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/commit/3df38af28729cadfa26c8a4ebe232ea5a48ca718) (from `package-lock.json`)

## Reproduction

1. `npm run dev`, open `/kitchen-sink/forms-chips.html#chip-input`
2. Click in the "Add more…" field of the *Chip input* example
3. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd>

Focus moves to the "TypeScript" chip (`document.activeElement` is the chip, `:focus-visible` matches, `.active` is not set). Its computed `outline-style` is `none` and `box-shadow` is `none`.

## Expected / Actual

- **Expected**: the focused chip shows a focus ring, like `.chip-dismiss` does.
- **Actual**: nothing marks the focused chip. The only visible ring belongs to the whole `.chip-input` (`:focus-within`), so you can't tell which chip has focus. Chips are selected (`.active`) on click and arrow keys, but not when Tab moves focus to them.

## Root cause

[`scss/_chip.scss#L59-L61`](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/blob/3df38af28729cadfa26c8a4ebe232ea5a48ca718/scss/_chip.scss#L59-L61):

```scss
&:focus-visible {
  outline: 0;
}
```

In the same file, `.chip-dismiss` pairs `outline: 0` with `@include focus-ring()` ([L133-L137](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/blob/3df38af28729cadfa26c8a4ebe232ea5a48ca718/scss/_chip.scss#L133-L137)). The chip itself doesn't. Chips are made focusable in [`js/src/chips.ts#L320`](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/blob/3df38af28729cadfa26c8a4ebe232ea5a48ca718/js/src/chips.ts#L320).

## Possible fix

Add a focus ring to `.chip:focus-visible`, the same way as `.chip-dismiss`:

```scss
&:focus-visible {
  outline: 0;
  @include focus-ring();
}
```

For now, the playground's home page works around it with a local outline on its filter chips (`src/home.css`).

body:
## Problem
`frontend/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts` computes the first/last focusable elements a single time when the trap activates. If the trapped container's contents change afterward (an accordion expands, an async section renders new inputs), the cached elements become stale.

## Impact

title: FocusTrap only focuses the first element on mount — it does not actually trap focus
body:
FocusTrap only focuses the first element on mount — it does not actually trap focus
`src/components/common/FocusTrap.tsx` queries focusable descendants and calls `.focus()` on the first one when `active` becomes true, but it has no `keydown` handler to cycle Tab/Shift+Tab within the container or prevent focus from escaping to the rest of the page.

Since this component is presumably used for modals (`Modal.tsx`, `ConfirmModal.tsx`), keyboard users can currently Tab out of an open modal into background content. Implement full cyclic focus trapping (or adopt a small tested library) and add a test.

## Additional Notes

**Correction on current usage**: as of this pass, `FocusTrap` is not actually consumed by `src/components/ui/Modal.tsx` (see the new issue "Modal has role=dialog/aria-modal but never traps or moves focus" filed in this same batch) — it's an existing, tested-in-isolation component that no dialog currently wires up. That makes this issue two-part: (1) fix `FocusTrap` itself to actually cycle Tab/Shift+Tab, and (2) actually adopt it in `Modal.tsx` and every confirm-dialog (`ConfirmModal`, `ConfirmEscrowModal`, `ConfirmSubscriptionModal`, `BatchConfirmModal`, and the Freighter-install prompt in `ConnectWallet.tsx`) so the fix has a real effect on the shipped app. Fixing only the component without wiring it up would leave the actual user-facing bug (tab-out-of-modal) unresolved.

**Implementation sketch**: add a `keydown` listener (attached while `active`) that on `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` re-queries focusable descendants (in case the DOM changed since mount — e.g. a form validation error appearing/disappearing changes the focusable set), and when focus is on the first/last element respectively, `preventDefault()` and move focus to the other end, forming a cycle. Also handle the case where `document.activeElement` is *not* inside the container at all when a key event fires (e.g. focus was moved out programmatically) by forcing it back to the first focusable element. On `active` transitioning back to `false`, restore focus to whatever element had focus before the trap activated (store it in a ref on mount).

**Edge cases**: a modal with zero focusable elements (rare, but e.g. a pure-content confirmation with no buttons yet while loading) — trap should fall back to focusing the container itself (`tabIndex={-1}`) rather than throwing on `elements[0].focus()` against an empty array; dynamically-added focusable elements after the initial mount (e.g. an inline validation "show password" toggle appearing) need the focusable-element query to happen live in the keydown handler, not just once on mount; nested modals (if any exist, e.g. a confirm-within-a-confirm) need trap stacking so only the topmost is active.

**Testing strategy**: `@testing-library/user-event`'s `.tab()` helper to simulate repeated Tab presses inside a rendered trap and assert focus cycles back to the first element after the last, and Shift+Tab cycles backward from the first to the last; a focus-restoration test asserting the pre-trap active element regains focus when `active` becomes false; an integration test on `Modal.tsx` once wired up, asserting Tab from the last focusable modal element does not move focus to a background page element.

**Cross-references**: directly blocks/complements the new issue about `Modal.tsx` not using `FocusTrap` at all — recommend implementing and merging both together, since a fixed-but-unused `FocusTrap` provides zero user-facing benefit on its own.

title: Modal never uses FocusTrap or restores focus — keyboard focus escapes open confirm dialogs for real money-moving actions
body:
## Problem

`Modal` — the shared component behind every confirmation dialog in the app, including the ones that trigger a real Freighter signing prompt for money-moving actions (`ConfirmModal`, `BatchConfirmModal`, `ConfirmEscrowModal`, `ConfirmSubscriptionModal`) — never traps keyboard focus inside itself, and never restores focus to the element that opened it.

The full list of what `Modal` does on open/close is scroll-locking and an Escape handler:

```tsx
// src/components/ui/Modal.tsx:40-59
useEffect(() => {
  if (isOpen) { document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden' } else { document.body.style.overflow = '' }
  return () => { document.body.style.overflow = '' }
}, [isOpen])

useEffect(() => {
  if (!isOpen || !onClose) return
  const handler = (e: KeyboardEvent) => { if (e.key === 'Escape') onClose() }
  document.addEventListener('keydown', handler)
  return () => document.removeEventListener('keydown', handler)
}, [isOpen, onClose])
```

There is no focus management at all: nothing moves focus into the dialog when it opens, nothing constrains `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` to the dialog's own focusable elements, and nothing returns focus to the trigger element when it closes. The app already has a purpose-built `FocusTrap` component (`src/components/common/FocusTrap.tsx`) — but `Modal.tsx` never imports or uses it:

```
$ grep -rln "FocusTrap" src --include="*.tsx"
src/components/common/FocusTrap.tsx
```

— only its own definition file. It is not used anywhere, including here.

## Why it matters

This is the shared dialog primitive for the highest-stakes interactions in the app: `ConfirmModal` (single send), `BatchConfirmModal` (batch send), `ConfirmEscrowModal` (locking funds), and `ConfirmSubscriptionModal` (authorizing a recurring payment) all render through `Modal`, all display a real amount and destination, and all lead directly to a Freighter signature request. For a keyboard-only or screen-reader user:
- `Tab`ing from the last focusable element inside the modal (e.g. the primary "Sign & Send" button) moves focus **out of the dialog and into the page content behind it** (the still-visible, still-`aria-hidden`-less `Card`/form/list underneath), even though the modal visually and semantically (`role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`) claims to be the only thing the user should be interacting with. A screen reader user tabbing past the last control has no indication they've left the dialog.
- On close (whether via Escape, backdrop click, or "Cancel"), focus is not returned anywhere — it's simply wherever it happened to land (often reset to `<body>`), so keyboard users lose their place in the underlying form entirely after cancelling a confirmation.
- This is functionally distinct from the already-filed bug in `FocusTrap` itself (which notes `FocusTrap` only focuses the first element on mount and doesn't actually trap subsequent Tab navigation): even a fixed `FocusTrap` would have zero effect here, because `Modal` doesn't wrap its children in `FocusTrap` at all.

## Reproduction

- Open any confirm modal (e.g. get to the review step of a Send and let the confirm modal render), then press `Tab` repeatedly from the "Cancel"/primary button. Focus moves onto elements in the page behind the modal (sidebar links, other buttons), while the modal remains visually open — `aria-modal="true"` notwithstanding.
- Close the modal via Escape and observe focus is not returned to whatever control opened it (e.g. the "Get Quote & Review" submit button).

## Suggested fix

- Wrap `Modal`'s content in `FocusTrap` (once `FocusTrap`'s own "only focuses first element" bug, filed separately in this repo, is fixed so it genuinely constrains `Tab`/`Shift+Tab`), or implement focus containment directly in `Modal` using the existing `overlayRef`.
- Capture `document.activeElement` in a ref when `isOpen` transitions to `true`, and call `.focus()` on it when `isOpen` transitions back to `false`, so focus returns to the triggering control on close.

## Additional Notes

The sign-in authentication dialog does not reliably contain keyboard focus. On `/sign-in`, initial focus remains on the underlying page/body instead of moving into the dialog, and continued Tab navigation can also reach `BODY` before reaching dialog controls. When the authentication dialog opens, keyboard focus should move to an appropriate interactive element within it and remain logically contained within the dialog while it is open. Keyboard users should not lose orientation by moving through the underlying page.

## Observed behavior
On `/sign-in`, when navigating the authentication dialog using the keyboard, initial focus remains on the underlying page/body instead of moving into the dialog. Continued Tab navigation can also reach `BODY` before reaching dialog controls. This was reproduced on both the Sign in and Sign up tabs.

title: fix(media): lightbox ignores Escape and arrow keys once Tab moves focus to <body>
body:
Found in exploratory testing against https://scadbuddy.internal.nullreference.io (main, `sha-30adee1`) with Playwright, 2026-10-04.

## What happens
The media lightbox (`MediaLightbox`, used on catalogue cards, list rows and the template page's gallery) stops answering the keyboard once Tab has moved focus out of it. Tab cycles through Close → Next → **`<body>`** → Close …. While focus is on `<body>`:
- **Escape does not close the lightbox**;
- **ArrowLeft and ArrowRight do not change the slide**.

The lightbox stays open over the page. The only way out is to Tab again, or to use the mouse.

What I measured, on a template with 4 media items (`qa-epic15-widgets`, now deleted):
- On the template page, opened from the gallery strip, the focus sequence was `DIV yarl__container` → `BUTTON Close` → `BUTTON Next` → `BODY` → `BUTTON Close` …. After 3 Tabs focus was on BODY. Escape then left `.yarl__root` in the DOM, and ArrowRight left the same caption showing.
- On the catalogue (`/?view=cards`), opened with a card's "View … full size" button, focus reached BODY after 4 Tabs, past the extra "Open template" link. Escape again left the lightbox open, and ArrowRight did nothing.
- On a video slide there are more controls, and 8 Tabs ended on BODY with the same result.

Before Tab reaches BODY, Escape and the arrow keys work.

## Repro
1. Open a template with 2 or more media items and click a gallery thumbnail (or a card's expand button on Models).
2. Press Tab until focus leaves the lightbox's buttons (3 times on the template page).
3. Press Escape. The lightbox stays open. Press → and the slide doesn't change.

## Cause (likely)
`frontend/src/components/media/LightboxView.tsx:40` renders `yet-another-react-lightbox`, whose keyboard handling listens on its own container. Its focus handling lets Tab reach `<body>` (the page behind is inert, so nothing else takes focus), and from there keydown never reaches the container. I didn't confirm this in the library's source.

## Expected
Focus stays inside the lightbox while it is open (a real focus trap). Or Escape and the arrow keys are handled at the document level while it is open, so they work wherever focus is.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Focusing the Preview panel via keybinding (workbench.panel.positronPreview.focus) causes subsequent keyboard shortcuts to stop working until mouse click
body:
When I use a keyboard shortcut bound to workbench.panel.positronPreview.focus (in my case cmd+3) to focus the Preview panel, other keybindings — e.g. cmd+1 (focus editor group) and cmd+2 (focus console) — stop responding afterward. They only start working again after I physically click into the editor or console with the mouse; pressing keys alone does not restore them. This suggests the Preview panel (a webview) is capturing/consuming keyboard events and not forwarding unhandled ones back to the main keybinding dispatcher, effectively trapping keyboard focus until a mouse click forces focus elsewhere. title: [A11y] General - Focus Visibility
body:
### Operating System

Windows

### Browser

Firefox

### Affected page

Homepage

### Admin user?

Yes

### Issue Description

Using Edge for most testing, I only just discovered that in Firefox some controls actually seem to be hiding focus indicators.  Edge seems to force a focus indicator around elements even when CSS would otherwise hide such an indicator, which is lovely for Edge users but awful for audits.

- The logo at the top has no focus indicator
- Whenever there's a "current" button (grid vs. list views), with the white on orange, it has no focus indicator
- Explore Collections has a focus indicator on the top buttons ("ALL", "OREGON STATE UNIVERSITY", etc.), but it fails to change anything other than color, and only barely.  I don't recall which WCAG area that fails, but it fails one of them....
- The fake dropdowns (e.g., "results per page") only change their border color and only slightly
- The "MY ACCOUNT" button might pass, I'm not sure, but when it's "pressed" it looks exactly the same as when it has focus, which is a separate kind of failure, so its focus should be indicated differently.
- On the "CREATE A NEW COLLECTION" modal, the visible focus indicator around "SAVE" is barely visible on Firefox.  The border changes almost imperceptibly, and the background color moves from a very dark blue to black.
- On the asset view page, the "FILE MANAGER" button has very little to indicate it's got focus, even with Edge trying its hardest to force a focus rectangle around it.

If this needs to be multiple tickets I can split that up, I'm just not sure which pieces will be easier to handle as a single change....

### Suggested Fix

Make sure keyboard focus is always very clear.  If there is a hover style, it's usually good to apply that, although in many of the above cases the hover style doesn't seem useful, either.

For something like the "grid" or "masonry" or "list" buttons, a 2px or so black border around the element would be fine.  For the buttons which already have borders around them, something a bit more drastic is required, like inverting the colors or else adding an inversion of the border, but with enough of the original border that it is noticeable and doesn't just get lost.  Edge does something like that and it seems okay, though I honestly have no idea how that's accomplished.

### Can anybody QA or does this need an expert?

Anybody

### QA Steps

Use Firefox and tab to every single control across all pages.  Make sure every single focusable element changes noticeably.  Test all modals, too.  Yeah, this won't be fun.

title: DataGrid: sort and column-menu icons are never revealed by keyboard focus
Active drawing mark cannot regain focus by clicking
body:
## Package

- lib-classifier

## Describe the bug

In drawing tasks without sub-tasks, once the active mark loses focus, it cannot be regained by clicking on the mark. 

## To Reproduce

1. Navigate to a suitable drawing task ([link](https://www.zooniverse.org/projects/met-rhonda/irish-weather-rescue/classify/workflow/28447/subject-set/131644/subject/113435303)).
2. Draw a line on the subject.
3. Cause the mark to lose focus, for example by clicking or tabbing away.
4. Click the mark again. Notice that the mark does not have focus - for example, you can't delete the mark by pressing 'backspace'.

## Expected behavior

Clicking a mark should cause it to gain focus.

## Device information

Ubuntu 20.04.6
Chrome 143, Firefox 136

## Additional context

- Note that this bug does not prevent a mark gaining focus by tabbing to it.
- Drawing tasks with sub-tasks are unaffected since clicking the mark opens the sub-task popup rather than focusing the mark (although it gains focus when the popup closes). 

- The issue here is that a mark does not lose its active status when it loses focus, unless focus is lost to another mark. For example, if a second line is drawn in the reproduction steps above, it is possible to transfer focus between the two lines by clicking them.
- This bug appears to be a regression introduced in #3817; the logic to deactivate the mark was (and still is) contained in the `onBlur` handler of the [DeleteButton](https://github.com/zooniverse/front-end-monorepo/blob/main/packages/lib-classifier/src/plugins/drawingTools/components/DeleteButton/DeleteButton.jsx). However, as the button can no longer receive keyboard focus, the handler doesn't run.

title: [Modal] Better focus management
body:
Current(master) focus-management is broken for shift+tab, while _forward tapping_ is also working not as expected, as long as you may leave a modal, and got into browser address line, which is good, but should be impossible.

A new `TrapFocus` implementation also does not seems to be correct, especially due to the absence of `RootRef`, used to discover nested portals (like here - https://nk7zmp3900.codesandbox.io/)

- [x] This is not a v0.x issue. 
- [x] I have searched the [issues](https://github.com/mui-org/material-ui/issues) of this repository and believe that this is not a duplicate.

## Expected Behavior 🤔
- loop then tabbing forward 
- loop then tabbing backwards 

## Current Behavior 😯
- loop then tabbing forward, with focus on body and modal after leaving browser address bar - causing 1 or 2 _tabs_ without visible response.
- does not loop backwards. A new `TrapFocus` would probably fix it, but might introduce other issues.

## Steps to Reproduce 🕹

See an example with 3 buttons inside a modal - https://codesandbox.io/s/j1ll74o3v9

## Context 🔦

Sorry, I have a professional deformation :) I've invested too much time in focus management, and all focus-related problems are _visible_ to me.

## Proposed solution

Replace `TrapFocus` by  [react-focus-lock](https://github.com/theKashey/react-focus-lock), which would handle all edge cases including Portals. There is only one downside of it - +4kb.

title: [Color] Focus ring color on inverted backgrounds
body:
### Provide a general summary of the issue here

**Description:**
Currently, the focus ring on inverted (bold) backgrounds uses color.border.inverted. This was introduced as a quick fix to guarantee sufficient contrast. Before that, the focus ring always used the regular focus color.

**Problem:**
The focus ring color now changes depending on the background, which may create inconsistency in how focus states are perceived across the system.
Ideally, focus indicators should remain consistent and recognizable, while still meeting accessibility contrast requirements.

**Questions to resolve:**
- Should the focus ring always use the same color for consistency, regardless of background?
- If yes, is our current focus color accessible enough on inverted/bold backgrounds?
- If not, should we define a dedicated alternative focus color (e.g., a lighter or darker tint of blue) for use on inverted backgrounds, instead of color.border.inverted?
- Do we want to introduce a specific token for focus rings on inverted backgrounds, or adjust the base focus ring token to cover this case?

**Next steps:**
Evaluate accessibility contrast of the current focus ring color on inverted backgrounds.
Explore potential alternatives (different tints of blue, or other consistent color solutions).
Decide whether to keep color.border.inverted or define a dedicated token.

DR

## Accessibility: color-contrast backlog

Follow-up to the Wave 7 mechanical a11y sweep (#368), which fixed alt/lang/heading/landmark issues and added a homepage axe smoke, but **deferred color-contrast** as design calls.

title: Quick Ask palette: selected row text contrast dropped to 3.7:1
body:
Follow-up to #454 (which lands the selection accent bar from #361).

## The problem

The selected Quick Ask row is now filled `0x987858`, and the row text is `0xE6E6E6`. That pair is about **3.7:1**, below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA asks for at the palette's 14 DIP normal-weight text. Before #454 it was about 9.3:1.

This is a spec problem, not a mistake in #454: #361 asked for the selected row to be at least 3:1 against the `0x262626` background, and with `E6E6E6` text no fill colour can meet both that and 4.5:1 for the text.

## The fix

- Let the 3px accent bar (`0xFFB080`, about 6.9:1 against `0x262626`) carry the "selection is visible" requirement.
- Change `selected_row_color()` in `src/ui/palette.rs` to a subtler tint so the row text stays at 4.5:1 or more.
- Update `selected_row_has_at_least_3_to_1_contrast_with_background` so it checks two pairs: accent bar vs background at 3:1 or more, and text vs selected row at 4.5:1 or more. Pulling the accent colour into a small function like `selected_row_color()` keeps the test and the drawing code from drifting apart.

## Done when

- The updated test passes, and it fails on the current `0x987858`.
- A before/after screenshot of the palette shows the selection still stands out and the text reads clearly.

A small, self-contained change: one file and one test, with no Win32 knowledge needed beyond changing a colour constant.

title: [Frontend] Theme System Architecture Refactor & High-Contrast Mode
body:
## Overview & Background
To provide an exceptional visual experience and meet strict WCAG AAA accessibility standards, the frontend theme engine needs a clean architecture refactor using semantic CSS variables, zero flash of unstyled theme (FOUT), and an official High-Contrast Mode for visually impaired users.

---

## Technical Specification & Architecture

1. **Semantic CSS Token System**:
   - Refactor `frontend/src/app/globals.css` with unified semantic design tokens:
     - `--color-bg-canvas`, `--color-bg-surface`, `--color-border-subtle`
     - `--color-text-primary`, `--color-text-secondary`, `--color-text-muted`
     - `--color-brand-primary`, `--color-brand-accent`
2. **High-Contrast Theme**:
   - Add `data-theme="high-contrast"` with bold black/white borders, yellow focus rings, and contrast ratios $> 7:1$.
3. **Theme Selector UI**:
   - Update `ModeToggle.tsx` to support: System, Light, Dark, and High Contrast.

---

## Target Files
- `frontend/src/app/globals.css`
- `frontend/src/components/ModeToggle.tsx`
- `frontend/src/context/theme-provider.tsx`

---

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Seamless theme switching with zero page flash on reload.
- [ ] High-contrast mode achieves $> 7:1$ contrast ratio across all UI elements.
- [ ] Clean semantic CSS variable structure.

title: Default palette: white on `success`, `primary` and `danger` fills, and light mode `success`, `warning` and `info` text, are under 4.5:1
body:
## Summary

With the default palette, several theme pairings are under WCAG AA's 4.5:1 for normal text. The worst is white text on `--success-bg` (solid buttons, badges and other `.theme-success` fills) at 2.82:1. In light mode, the `fg` text colors of `warning`, `info` and `success` on `--bg-body` are under 4.5:1 too.

## Bootstrap version

`v6-dev` at [`bd0a4f6`](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/commit/bd0a4f63ce5cc444063c28a6946bdae3dacdce20)

## Reproduction

Open the Button kitchen sink page (`kitchen-sink/components-button.html`) with the `default` config. Measure the contrast between each theme's `--<theme>-bg` and `--<theme>-contrast` (solid fills), and between its `--<theme>-fg` and `--bg-body` (colored text), in light and dark mode. Colors are resolved in the browser and gamut-mapped to sRGB before the WCAG 2 formula.

| Theme | `bg` / `contrast` | `fg` / `bg-body`, light | `fg` / `bg-body`, dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `primary` | **3.56** | 5.38 | 7.25 |
| `accent` | 5.30 | 7.59 | 6.75 |
| `success` | **2.82** | **4.34** | 8.50 |
| `danger` | **4.42** | 6.51 | 6.32 |
| `warning` | 11.32 | **3.96** | 14.04 |
| `info` | 7.39 | **3.71** | 9.89 |
| `inverse` | 17.47 / 16.29 | 17.47 | 12.13 |
| `secondary` | 13.81 / 5.85 | 5.85 | 6.92 |

`bg` / `contrast` doesn't depend on the mode for the chromatic themes: `bg` is the `500` step and `contrast` is white or `--gray-900` in both.

## Expected

The default solid fills and text colors meet 4.5:1, or the docs say which pairings are for large or bold text only.

## Actual

White on `--success-bg`, `--primary-bg` and `--danger-bg` and, in light mode, `--success-fg`, `--warning-fg` and `--info-fg` on the body background are under 4.5:1.

## Root cause

[`scss/_theme.scss`](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/blob/bd0a4f63ce5cc444063c28a6946bdae3dacdce20/scss/_theme.scss): `bg` is the `500` step for every chromatic theme, and `contrast` is fixed per theme (`var(--white)` or `var(--gray-900)`). With [`$green: oklch(64% .22 160)`](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/blob/bd0a4f63ce5cc444063c28a6946bdae3dacdce20/scss/_colors.scss#L23) and [`$blue: oklch(60% .24 240)`](https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/blob/bd0a4f63ce5cc444063c28a6946bdae3dacdce20/scss/_colors.scss#L13), a 500 step is too light for white text. Light mode's `fg` is the `600` step (`700` for `warning`), which isn't dark enough for green, yellow and cyan.

## Possible fix

Darken the `bg` of the light hues (`bg: var(--green-600)`) or switch their `contrast` to `--gray-900`, and use the `700` step for the light mode `fg` of `success` and `info` (and `800` for `warning`). A check in the docs' build that computes these ratios would keep them from regressing.

## Refinement (what to build here)

Everything this issue measures is already covered by the playground, so the remaining work is a dedicated reproduction page that can be linked upstream:

- **Existing coverage**: [`pages/contrast.html`](https://github.com/julien-deramond/bootstrap-test-playground/blob/main/pages/contrast.html) measures every pairing above (`<theme> contrast on bg`, `btn-solid`, `badge`, `<theme> fg on bg-body`, `fg on bg-subtle`, subtle/outline/text variants), and `npm run test:a11y -- -g "contrast default"` lists the failing ones. They are allowlisted under this issue in `tests/a11y/known-issues.js` (the `pairing-contrast` entries and the `color-contrast` entries by color pair). The `--success-fg` on `--bg-2` and `--fg-3` on `--bg-2` cases from the comment are in the same file.
- **To add**: `issues/pg-183/` (`npm run new-issue pg-183 -- --config default`), a single page that shows each failing pairing (solid fills with their `contrast` text, and light/dark `fg` text on the body) with its measured WCAG 2 ratio, so the problem is visible without the full contrast page. Its `assert.js` resolves the colors the way the table above does (computed color, gamut-mapped to sRGB) and returns `pass: true` only when every default solid fill and every `fg`

title: Flaky: large-text audits report contrast on sheet bar buttons while they appear; Markup menu tap swallowed
body:
## What happens

`integration` went red at 1b6151a (#74). The code hadn't changed; the failures are in the large-text journeys added by #72.

- **`testTheLibraryScanningAndSettingsAtALargeTextSize`** fails its audit on a sheet's navigation-bar text button, and the button differs from run to run:
  - [run 36696742664](https://github.com/Algorythmos-AI/pdf-algo-pro/actions/runs/36696742664) (`integration`): "Contrast failed" on **Done** (307,82) in Settings, plus one "Potentially inaccessible text" finding with no element.
  - #75's run: "Contrast failed" on **Cancel** (20,82) in the scan sheet.
- **`testTheSignatureSheetAtALargeTextSize`** fails because "Signature" isn't found after tapping Markup. The UI hierarchy saved at the failure shows the reader with the menu closed, so the tap on Markup didn't open it.
- **Passed:** the previous head, 1b96264, and #72's own run, with the same tree.

## Likely cause

- **Contrast.** The accent colour (#6D28D9) is about 7:1 against white, so a drawn button can't fail. On iOS 26 a sheet's bar buttons sit on Liquid Glass that finishes appearing after the sheet itself. The audit measured the button while it was still appearing. This is the same kind of timing as #69 and #44.
- **Signature.** The Markup tap arrived while the reader was still settling after launch, and the test didn't wait for the menu before tapping an item in it.

## Fix

- The audit now waits for the screen to be still for half a second (three matching screenshots) rather than a quarter.
- Contrast findings on buttons inside navigation bars, and "Potentially inaccessible text" findings with no element, are quarantined as a non-strict expected failure that links here (docs/testing-strategy.md, Flaky tests). Contrast anywhere else still fails.
- Menus are opened with a helper that waits for the menu item and taps the menu button once more if the first tap was swallowed.

## To do, by 2026-10-07 (five business days)

- [ ] Five consecutive green CI runs.
- [ ] Remove the quarantine if the stricter wait alone keeps it green. Otherwise record the debt and keep the quarantine with evidence from the audit screenshots.

title: fix(a11y): colour alone distinguishes vibe and persona categories
body:
The wrapped experience categorizes activity into vibes and personas, which are presented through colour. Where colour is the only distinguishing signal, the categorization is lost for colour-blind users and in the greyscale rendering of a shared image.

**Scope:**
- Audit where category is conveyed by colour alone and add a second signal: a label, an icon, or a pattern.
- Check the contrast of text over the category colours and over the share card's gradients, which is where contrast failures usually sit.
- Verify the share card remains legible in greyscale, since shared images are reproduced in contexts you do not control.
- Include the check in the automated accessibility pass.

**Done when:** no category depends on colour alone and contrast passes on every surface including the card.

title: Make default media alt-text configurable
body:
**Overview of feature request**

Currently, Islandora's approach to generating alt-text on media is to default to title, in this function: https://github.com/Islandora/islandora/blob/2.x/islandora.module#L530-L552

Request: instead of hard-coding the title as the source of the default, make it configurable, so that any field (i.e. Description) from the Repository Item content type can be used.
 
**What kind of user is the feature intended for?**

Anyone who ingests objects; also can improve accessibility (by providing a useful default for alt-text, images that aren't given manual alt-text will receive something more helpful).
 
 
**What inspired the request?**
 
Received questions about accessibility from one of our admins as we prepare to migrate to modern Islandora. Found this note in the [documentation](https://islandora.github.io/documentation/user-documentation/accessibility/):

> Automatic alt-text
> When creating image media, alt-text is a required attribute. An Islandora function currently automatically populates the alt-text, if that media is the "media of" a node, with the respective node's title.
> This is not considered good accessibility as the node's title will likely be already on the page, and it doesn't add anything to describing the image itself. Please fill out the alt text with something meaningful when adding image content to Islandora.

Configurable default fields would improve (though not fully resolve) accessibility behaviour.
 
**What existing behavior do you want changed?**
 
Change the default behaviour when uploading media for an Islandora object (currently uses nodeTitle by default unless handmade alt text is provided); add configuration to specify a Drupal field as the source for default alt text.

title: Markdown viewer: broken-image placeholder + alt-text accessibility (tooltip, a11y tree)
body: ## Problem When an image in the Markdown viewer fails to load (missing local file, unreachable remote URL, decode failure), the result is a completely borderless, contentless box at the computed size — no broken-image icon, no alt text, no visual signal at all. The reader can't distinguish "image failed" from intentional blank space. This applies identically to markdown images (`[image]`) and raw-HTML `` (#13721) — they share the same render path. ## Current state The rendering machinery already supports exactly the affordance needed: `warpui_core`'s `Image` element has a `failed_to_load` backup-element hook (`crates/warpui_core/src/elements/gui/image.rs:179`) that paints an arbitrary element inside the image's box on load failure — but no consumer in the codebase sets it, and no broken-image icon asset exists yet. ## Suggested fix - A modest placeholder element — broken-image glyph, optionally accompanied by the image's alt text (which is parsed and carried today but never displayed) — set via the existing `failed_to_load` hook in the shared `RenderableImage` (`crates/editor/src/render/element/image.rs`), so markdown and HTML images gain it together. - Browsers render a broken-image icon + alt text in this situation; that's the reader expectation being violated. ## Acceptance criteria (added 2026-07-20 — accessibility is a first-class part of this feature) Alt text should behave per standard browser expectations, not just decorate the failure case: - Failed loads render a broken-image glyph plus the image's alt text in the available box; a generic "Image failed to load" notice when alt is empty/whitespace. - Hovering an image with non-empty alt text — loaded or failed — shows the alt text as a tooltip. - Images with non-empty alt text are exposed to the accessibility tree with the alt text as their accessible name (image role). Images with empty alt (`[image]`) are decorative and must be **omitted** from the accessibility tree, matching browser `alt=""` semantics. ## Related Part of the raw-HTML/markdown viewer effort: #13652, #13721 (whose spec documents the current empty-box behavior explicitly as inherited, with this affordance called out as a possible follow-up).

title: Imagery - Alt Text
body:
**Requirement**: All images must carry alt tags.

**Why is this required?** If an image is published without an alt tag then a screen reader would inform the user that there is an image on the page, but would not be able to give them any information about it, causing frustration.

**Exceptions**: If images are decorative or a background CSS image, then the alt tag must be left empty (i.e. alt=””).This tells the screen reader to skip the image. If an image has a caption with a sufficient description, then it is acceptable to leave the alt tag empty.

**Requirement**: when image links are adjacent to text links to the same destination, the image and text links MUST be combined and an empty alt tag
used. 

**Why is this required?** This reduces the number of links that screenreader users and keyboard users have to navigate

title: Support alt text for inline math
body:
Pandoc does not allow alt text for inline equations, at the AST level.

This may be a temporary issue because UA-2 does much smarter MathML interpretation of equations, where you no longer need alt text. 

But there will be a transitionary period, as seen in
* https://github.com/orgs/quarto-dev/discussions/14119

where some tools and readers may still need UA-1 alt text for equations, even when UA-2 mathml is available.

LaTeX implements UA-2, and it's highly likely that Typst will implement UA-2 later this year.

q2 support free-floating attribute blocks, so this is directly fixable with no new syntax there. For Pandoc we'd need to invent a new syntax. ☹️ 

## Description

Quarto currently supports alt text for display math equations via `{#eq-label alt="..."}` (added in #13889), but there is no mechanism for adding alt text to **inline math** expressions. This causes PDF/UA-1 validation failures when documents contain inline math like `$a$`, `$f(x)$`, or `$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$` in Typst output.

Typst's PDF/UA-1 mode requires every `math.equation` element (including inline) to have an `alt` parameter. Without a way to specify this from Quarto markdown, any document with inline math will fail UA-1 validation.

## Current state

- **Display math with labels**: ✅ Supported via `{#eq-label alt="..."}`
- **Display math without labels**: ❌ No mechanism
- **Inline math**: ❌ No mechanism

## Steps to Reproduce

```qmd
---
format:
  typst:
    pdf-standard: ua-1
---

For a right triangle with legs $a$ and $b$ and hypotenuse $c$: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$
```

Each inline math expression produces: `error: PDF/UA-1 error: missing alt text`

## Impact

In testing Quarto book extensions (bookly, ilm, wonderous-book) with `pdf-standard: ua-1`, after fixing all image and display equation alt text, the **only remaining errors** are inline math — 30 errors per project, all from theorem/definition content containing inline variables and formulas.

## Possible approaches

1. **Span syntax**: Allow `[$a$]{alt="a"}` to propagate the `alt` attribute to the generated Typst `math.equation`
2. **Auto-generation**: Automatically generate alt text from the math source (e.g., `$a$` → `alt: "a"`, `$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$` → `alt: "a^2 + b^2 = c^2"`) — the LaTeX/Typst source is often a reasonable alt text for simple expressions
3. **Global show rule**: Emit a Typst show rule like `show math.equation: set math.equation(alt: ...)` if the document uses `pdf-standard: ua-1` — though Typst currently doesn't support setting `alt` via show rules

Note: Typst plans to support MathML-based accessibility in PDF 2.0 which would make manual alt text unnecessary, but for PDF/UA-1 the `alt` parameter is the only option.

title: SegmentedControl: accept aria-labelledby and align subcomponent names with DOM
body:
## 💡 Suggestion

Two related improvements to `SegmentedControl` around accessible naming and subcomponent naming.

### 1. Accessible name: require `aria-label` **or** `aria-labelledby`

`SegmentedControl.List` currently types `'aria-label'` as a **required** `string`:

```ts
export interface SegmentedControlListProps<T = any>
  extends Omit<Partial<ExtractProps<typeof Grid, never>>, 'children'> {
  'aria-label': string;
  children: ((item: T) => React.ReactNode) | React.ReactNode;
}
```

(`modules/react/segmented-control/lib/SegmentedControlList.tsx`)

The rendered node is a `div` with `role="group"`. A group needs an accessible name. Both of these are valid:

- `aria-label="Density"`
- `aria-labelledby={headingId}` pointing at a visible heading / label

Using only `aria-labelledby` is a TypeScript error even though it is correct ARIA (`aria-labelledby` wins when both are present). That pushes examples toward duplicating the visible label in `aria-label`.

**Proposal:** Type the accessible name as **one of** `aria-label: string` **or** `aria-labelledby: string`. Do not require both. Docs can still recommend `aria-label` when there is no visible group name.

Runtime already accepts `aria-labelledby`; this is mainly a type (and docs) fix. It is only a TS break if we stop requiring `aria-label` when `aria-labelledby` is set.

### 2. Rename `List` / `Item` to match the DOM

`SegmentedControl.List` does **not** render a list. It renders a `div` with `role="group"` (docs compare this to a fieldset). `SegmentedControl.Item` does **not** render a list item. It renders a `<button>` (`BaseButton`) with `aria-pressed`.

`List` / `Item` imply `ul`/`ol` + `li` (or `role="list"` / `listitem`), which this pattern is not.

**Proposal (breaking, `prerelease/major`):** rename to match what they render:

| Current | Renders | Proposed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SegmentedControl.List` | `div` + `role="group"` | `SegmentedControl.Group` |
| `SegmentedControl.Item` | `<button>` | `SegmentedControl.Button` |

Keep aliases or a codemod so existing `List` / `Item` usage can migrate.

## Motivation

- Visible headings should be allowed to name the group via `aria-labelledby` (Density example: an `h3` plus the control).
- Requiring `aria-label` when a visible label already exists encourages redundant or conflicting names (**no ARIA is better than bad ARIA**).
- Names that match the DOM (`Group` + `Button`) make the keyboard/SR story easier to teach.

## Example

Preferred when a visible name already exists:

```tsx
<Text as="h3" id={densityLabelId}>
  Density
</Text>
<SegmentedControl initialValue={density} onSelect={handleDensity} size="small">
  <SegmentedControl.List aria-labelledby={densityLabelId}>
    <SegmentedControl.Item data-id="high">High</SegmentedControl.Item>
    <SegmentedControl.Item data-id="medium">Medium</SegmentedControl.Item>
    <SegmentedControl.Item data-id="low">Low</SegmentedControl.Item>
  </SegmentedControl.List>
</SegmentedControl>
```

Today this fails type-checking unless `aria-label` is also passed.

After a rename (major):

```tsx
<SegmentedControl.Group aria-labelledby={densityLabelId}>
  <SegmentedControl.Button data-id="high">High</SegmentedControl.Button>
</SegmentedControl.Group>
```

## Context

- Docs already describe `role="group"` and treat `aria-label` as **recommended**, not exclusive of `aria-labelledby`: `modules/react/segmented-control/stories/SegmentedControl.mdx`.
- Hit this while updating `modules/react/_examples/stories/mdx/examples/Density.tsx`.

Three things on the History and Library pages that a screen reader (or a buttons list, e.g. VoiceOver rotor or NVDA Insert+F7) can't tell apart. ## 1. History: every row's actions have the same names On `/m/qa-explore-cube/history` (4–5 outputs), the accessibility tree has N × `button "Edit"`, N × `button "Send again"` and N × `button "Delete"`, none tied to the output id (e80a0163, d63bce4a…). In a list of buttons they're indistinguishable. Compare the preset row, which already uses "Delete preset ‹name›". Code: `frontend/src/pages/HistoryPage.tsx` ~line 330–340 on main. ## 2. History: the parameter diff reads as one number For an output with side 21 (default 20), the `
` is `2120`. The accessibility tree exposes `definition: "2120"`. The strike-through is CSS only, so "was 20" is lost and the two values run together. Code: same file ~line 351–355. Use ``/`` or visually-hidden text ("21, default 20"). ## 3. Library: every card's button is just "Print", and the open folder isn't exposed On `/library`, each card's action is `button "Print"` with no `aria-label` or `aria-describedby` naming the file (`LibraryPage.tsx` ~line 156), and the thumbnails have `alt=""`. In the "Library folders" nav, the current folder is shown only by a background (`bg-accent/8`). No button has `aria-current` or `aria-pressed`, so there's no way to tell which folder is open. Folder counts are also run together with the name ("MakerWorld49", "Tst55") because the count span has no separator or label. ## Expected - Contextual names, e.g. `aria-label="Delete output e80a0163"`, or `aria-describedby` pointing at the row's id or file name. - `aria-current="true"` on the selected folder. - Separated or labelled counts ("MakerWorld, 49 files"). Related: #935 (visually telling identically named library files apart). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: a11y(web): Select inside Field is named by its placeholder, not the field label (rc.2 regression of #570)
body:
## Summary
On `0.86.2-rc.2`, a `Select` inside a `Field` is no longer associated with the field label at all. The double accessible name from #570 is gone, but the combobox is now named by its placeholder, so a screen reader announces the placeholder and never the field label. `Input` inside `Field` is correct.

## Reproduction (Web, Chromium, BeePOS probe route)
```tsx
<Field required>
  <FieldLabel>Cửa hàng nhận</FieldLabel>
  <Select value={v} onValueChange={setV}>
    <SelectTrigger><SelectValue placeholder="Chọn cửa hàng" /></SelectTrigger>
    <SelectContent>{/* items */}</SelectContent>
  </Select>
</Field>
```
- `page.getByLabel('Cửa hàng nhận')` returns **0** elements (rc.1 returned 2, which is what #570 reported)
- The combobox has `aria-label="Chọn cửa hàng"` and no `aria-labelledby`
- Accessibility snapshot: `combobox "Chọn cửa hàng"`, while the label text sits in a plain generic node
- Control in the same Field layout: `Input` gets `aria-labelledby` and `getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Tên sản phẩm' })` returns 1

## Cause (from the published source)
`SelectTrigger` does not read the field context; its fallback accessible name is the placeholder.

## Suggested fix
Have `SelectTrigger` consume the Field context the way `Input` does (`aria-labelledby` to the FieldLabel, `aria-describedby` to description/error, `aria-required`, `aria-invalid`), and use the placeholder only when no label exists. Add a Playwright check `getByLabel(<field label>)` = 1 for Select, as there is for Input.

Regression of #570 (Select case). Found by BeePOS rc.2 verification (2026-09-23). Tracked in #234.

title: Accessibility: Improve search input accessibility with ARIA labels and descriptions
body:
**Issue Description**  
The search input currently lacks proper accessibility attributes making it difficult for screen readers and keyboard users to navigate efficiently. Without ARIA labels and descriptions blind users may struggle to understand the purpose of the search field impacting their ability to explore content seamlessly. This issue affects accessibility compliance and overall user experience particularly for those relying on assistive technologies.  

 **Proposed Solution**  
- Add `aria-label="Search articles"` to provide clear identification for screen readers  
- Use `aria-describedby` to link a help text that explains search functionality and available options  
- Ensure proper association between the input field and its corresponding help text for better usability  

 **Benefits**  
- **Enhances screen reader compatibility** making navigation easier for blind and visually impaired users  
- **Improves keyboard accessibility** ensuring all users can interact with the search function efficiently  
- **Aligns with accessibility standards** such as WCAG fostering a more inclusive experience  

 **Implementation**  
- Add appropriate ARIA attributes to the search input field  
- Include a clear descriptive help text to assist users  
- Maintain existing functionality while significantly improving accessibility  

**PRs**  
PR #1313 implements these critical accessibility improvements.

title: Accessibility pass on console pages without ARIA
body:
## Summary

```sh
npm --prefix web run build
npm --prefix web test
```
passes. Include a before/after note (or axe results) in the PR.

title: Add aria-labels to FileTreePanel action buttons
body:
## Summary
The file-tree header in `FileTreePanel` has a cluster of icon-only `ActionIcon` buttons (search, new file, new folder, upload, refresh) that have visual tooltips but no `aria-label`, so they expose no accessible name. Add i18n-backed `aria-label`s to each.

## Background
`FileTreePanel` renders the workspace sidebar's file tree, including a toolbar of icon-only actions. Each button is wrapped in a Mantine `Tooltip` with a translated label, but a tooltip is visual-only and is not announced as the button's accessible name. The fix is to add an `aria-label` to each `ActionIcon`, reusing the translation key already passed to its surrounding `Tooltip` — no new locale keys are required. All five toolbar keys already exist in both `en/chat.json` and `zh/chat.json` under `chat.workspace.*`.

Note: the per-file "delete" button is NOT in this file — it lives in the row component `skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/components/FileTreeItem.tsx` (around line 160, the `IconTrash` `ActionIcon`). This issue scopes to the header cluster in `FileTreePanel/index.tsx`; the delete button can be handled the same way if desired, but is out of scope unless you choose to include it.

## Affected code
- `skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx:160` — search toggle (`IconSearch`), `Tooltip` label `t('chat.workspace.searchFiles')` ([link](https://github.com/SkeinAI/Skein/blob/main/skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx#L160))
- `skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx:174` — new file (`IconFilePlus`), `Tooltip` label `t('chat.workspace.newFile')` ([link](https://github.com/SkeinAI/Skein/blob/main/skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx#L174))
- `skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx:189` — new folder (`IconFolderPlus`), `Tooltip` label `t('chat.workspace.newFolder')` ([link](https://github.com/SkeinAI/Skein/blob/main/skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx#L189))
- `skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx:204` — upload (`IconUpload`), `Tooltip` label `t('chat.workspace.uploadFile')` ([link](https://github.com/SkeinAI/Skein/blob/main/skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx#L204))
- `skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx:215` — refresh (`IconRefresh`), `Tooltip` label `t('chat.workspace.refresh')` ([link](https://github.com/SkeinAI/Skein/blob/main/skein-ui/src/pages/Workspace/components/FileTreePanel/index.tsx#L215))

## Implementation steps
1. For each of the five `ActionIcon`s above, add an `aria-label` prop reusing the same translation key already used by its enclosing `Tooltip`:
   - search → `aria-label={t('chat.workspace.searchFiles')}`
   - new file → `aria-label={t('chat.workspace.newFile')}`
   - new folder → `aria-label={t('chat.workspace.newFolder')}`
   - upload → `aria-label={t('chat.workspace.uploadFile')}`
   - refresh → `aria-label={t('chat.workspace.refresh')}`
2. No locale changes are needed: all five keys already exist in `skein-ui/src/i18n/locales/en/chat.json` and `skein-ui/src/i18n/locales/zh/chat.json` under the `workspace` object.
3. (Optional, if you choose to extend scope) Apply the same `aria-label` pattern to the delete `ActionIcon` in `FileTreeItem.tsx`; it currently has no tooltip/label, so it would need a new key (e.g. `chat.workspace.deleteFile`) added to both locale files.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All five header `ActionIcon`s in `FileTreePanel/index.tsx` have an i18n-backed `aria-label`.
- [ ] `aria-label` values reuse the existing `chat.workspace.*` keys (no new keys required for the header cluster).
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes with no new errors.

## How to verify
```
cd skein-ui && npm run lint
```
Manual: run `npm run tauri dev`, open a workspace so the file tree shows, and inspect each toolbar button in browser devtools — every `<button>` should expose an `aria-label

title: Associate field messages with their input via aria-describedby (message text currently folds into the accessible name)
body:
**Deferred — not MVP.**

The crate emits no `aria-describedby` anywhere. Field messages are associated with their input only by being rendered *inside* the wrapping `<label>`, which has two consequences, one of them a real defect.

## The defect: error text folds into the accessible name

`Input`, `Textarea` and `Select` all render

```
label.form-field
  span.field-label      <- the caption
  input / textarea / select
  FieldErrors           <- ul.field-errors
```

An `<input>` wrapped in a `<label>` gets its accessible name from that label's subtree text content, minus the input itself. The `ul` of messages is in that subtree, so the field's accessible name becomes something like *"Title This field is required."* rather than *"Title"*. The required marker escapes this only because it carries `aria-hidden="true"`.

So the name changes when validation runs, and the message is announced as part of the field's identity rather than as its description.

`Checkbox` has the same shape when it has a label (`FieldErrors` sits in the fragment that gets wrapped). `RadioGroup` is **not** affected: its `FieldErrors` is a child of the `fieldset`, and a fieldset's accessible name comes from its `legend` specifically, not from all descendant text.

**Confirm this in a real browser before fixing.** It follows from the accname text-content rules, but it is cheap to verify and worth verifying: assert on the accessible name with `get_by_role` in the `e2e` crate, which is the only place that can see a computed name (see `.claude/memory/e2e_harness.md`). A test that pins the name of an errored field is the regression guard for the fix either way.

## The fix

Give the message list an id derived from the field path and point the input at it:

```
ul.field-errors  id="{path}-errors"
input            aria-describedby="{path}-errors"
```

Only when messages exist — a dangling `aria-describedby` is itself a defect. That is one more thing derived from the same "are there messages" bit that `aria_invalid` already comes from, so it resolves at the same boundary and rides in `FieldProps` the same way (see `FieldProps::aria_invalid`).

Note the ids are the first ids formoxus would emit, so path characters need checking — `x.y[0].z` contains `.` and `[]`, which are legal in an HTML id but need escaping in a CSS selector. Test selectors should use `get_by_role`, not `#id`.

## Why it matters more once warnings exist

#8 adds non-blocking messages. Those are *descriptions* in the strictest sense — the field is valid, and the text is advice. Folded into the accessible name, a warning would permanently rename the field, which is worse than the error case because nothing the user does clears it.

## Keep the current placement

The `ul` stays where it is in the DOM. Its position as an immediate sibling is what lets a plain `input[aria-invalid="true"] + *` selector reach it with no framework and no class, which `FieldErrors`'s doc comment records as deliberate. `aria-describedby` fixes the semantics without moving anything.

title: Truncate long labels in session quickpick with tooltip and aria label
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #11896. Notebook session labels in the interpreter picker are based off the filename, which can be really long and cause the interpreter picker width to grow since there's no max-width cap. A long filename plus a small window size can cause contents in the top action bar to get cut off. We should limit the width of the interpreter picker so it can't cause any content to be cut-off at the smallest allowed window width.

We should: 
1. Truncate the interpreter picker label using the same truncation logic the Explorer pane uses for long filenames
2. Show the full, untruncated label in a hover tooltip
3. Expose the full label via an `aria-label` so screen readers announce it in full (along with the current session status)

title: Post-1.0: three accessibility and translation leftovers from #671
body:
Post-1.0. Three small leftovers from #671 (global UI cleanup), found while reviewing it after it merged. The functional fixes from the same review are in #681. None of these blocks v1. Line numbers are at rock `e55f3b4`.

## 1. The first vanity estimate may not be announced

`#vanity-estimate` (`src/shell.html:320`) is an `aria-live="polite"` region that now starts `hidden`. `hodlVanityEstimate` (`src/js/app.js:16079`, `:16083`) shows it and fills it in the same step. Screen readers often skip a live region that enters the accessibility tree together with its first content. So the first estimate after a valid prefix can go unannounced. Later updates, while it is visible, are announced.

**Fix:** keep the live region rendered all the time, and hide only the grey note box while it is empty. For example, put `aria-live` on an always-present wrapper and the edge-note styling on an inner element.

**Acceptance:**
- Typing a valid prefix announces its first estimate.
- An empty estimate still draws no box.

## 2. The banner's dismiss button still says "beta software"

The banner's title is now "Experimental software" (`src/shell.html:28`). Its dismiss button is still `aria-label="Dismiss the beta software warning"` (`src/shell.html:29`), so screen-reader users hear a different name than sighted users read.

**Fix:** reword the label to match, for example "Dismiss the experimental software warning". The translation workflow picks it up after merge.

## 3. Copy-icon labels switch to English after a copy

`showCopiedIcon` (`src/js/clipboard.js:45`) sets the button's `aria-label` and `title` from its `label` and `copiedLabel` options. Those default to English "Copy" and "Copied", and nothing passes them through `t()`. Both callers rely on that:
- **Expand overlay** (`src/js/expandable.js:134`): in de, es, fr and pt its icon starts out translated, because the static `aria-label="Copy"` (`expandable.js:74`) is built before the boot sweep. From the first copy on, it reads English.
- **Reference QR popup** (`src/js/qr-references.js:73`): passes `label: "Copy URL"` in English.

Related, and older than #671: the reference QR popup builds its whole card (the scan hint, Copy URL, Close) each time it opens, after the boot sweep, and `qr-references.js` has no `t()`. So that popup is English in every locale.

**Fix:**
- Have both callers pass translated labels: `t("Copy")`, `t("Copied")`, `t("Copy URL")`. `clipboard.js` doesn't need `t()` itself.
- Build the reference QR popup's card text with `t()`.

**Acceptance:**
- In a non-English locale, both copy icons keep a translated label before and after a copy.
- The reference QR popup's text is translated.

Drafted with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5).

title: bug(web a11y): Field exposes the accessible name on both the label element and the control, so getByLabel resolves to 2 nodes
body:
## Problem
On Web, `Field` renders its label element with `aria-label="<label>, required"` and also passes the same name to the child control (e.g. `role="combobox" aria-label="<label>"`). Two nodes therefore expose the field's accessible name. Any standards-based "control named X" query resolves to two elements: Playwright `page.getByLabel('Cửa hàng nhận')` throws a strict-mode violation on every `Field` + `Select`/`Input` composition, and assistive-tech "find control named X" behaves the same way.

## Repro
```tsx
<Field label="Cửa hàng nhận" required><Select ...>...</Select></Field>
```
Web: `page.getByLabel('Cửa hàng nhận')` resolves to 2 elements.

## Suggested fix
Drop the redundant `aria-label` from the label element (the label/control association already carries the name), or mark the label as presentational for name computation, matching native `<label for>` semantics. Related a11y reports from the BeeECOM audit: #546, #559.

---
Found by the **BeePOS** consumer field audit (Hive Enterprise), an external Expo SDK 57 + expo-router app consuming `@beemvp/beeui-ui@0.86.2-rc.1` from npm: https://github.com/beobungbu/BeePOS (findings under `docs/beeui-audit/`). Tracked in #234.

title: Implement the ARIA tabs pattern on the artist profile tab strip
body:
## Description

The profile tab strip is a `<nav>` containing three plain buttons with no tab semantics and no keyboard navigation, and the panel is not focusable. Screen-reader users hear three anonymous buttons and must Tab through all of them to reach the active panel.

**Where it lives**

`src/features/profile/pages/ArtistProfilePage.tsx:111-143` (the tab strip: no `role="tablist"`, no `role="tab"`, no `aria-selected`, no `id`/`aria-controls`, no roving `tabIndex`, no Arrow/Home/End handling), `:147-152` (the panel has no `role="tabpanel"`, no `aria-labelledby`, no `tabIndex={0}`). Also `:25-39` injects a `<meta name="description">` into `<head>` and never removes it, so navigating artist → artist leaks the previous artist's description. Related: the tab state is already deep-linked via `useSearchParams` at `:17,47`.

**Why it matters**

The artist profile is the app's most important public page, and its primary navigation is unusable with a screen reader or by keyboard alone.

## Suggested Direction

Add `role="tablist"` to the nav (or switch to a `<div role="tablist">` with an appropriate label), `role="tab" aria-selected={isActive} aria-controls={panelId} id={tabId}` and `tabIndex={isActive ? 0 : -1}` to each button, and an `onKeyDown` implementing Arrow Left/Right, Home and End. Give the panel `role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby={activeTabId} tabIndex={0}`. Generate ids with `useId()`. Separately, return a cleanup from the meta-description effect so the tag is removed on unmount.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The strip exposes `role="tablist"` and each control exposes `role="tab"` with `aria-selected`
- [ ] Arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs and follow the roving-`tabIndex` pattern
- [ ] The panel is `role="tabpanel"`, is labelled by its tab, and is focusable
- [ ] Navigating between two artists does not leave the previous artist's meta description in the document
- [ ] Tests added/updated and passing (`npm run test`)
- [ ] Docs updated if behavior changes (`README.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` as applicable)

title: [Feature] 面板无障碍批次一：aria-live / 焦点管理 / 逐项标注 / 图表摘要
body:
## 背景

对面板前端做了第一遍 WCAG 导向审计。骨架及格：按钮/输入框基本都有 aria-label、装饰图标统一 aria-hidden、星级评分有 role="img"+数值标签、会话列表用 tree/treeitem 语义、大弹层有 role="region"+aria-label+Esc 关闭、开关控件有 aria-checked/aria-expanded。

系统性缺口（按 WCAG 四原则）：

| 缺口 | 位置 | 原则 |
|---|---|---|
| 状态变化无播报 | 保存成功/失败、队列刷新、resolve 完成——纯视觉 span，无 aria-live | 可感知 |
| 操作缺上下文 | 冲突队列「保留 A」读屏只听到「保留 A」，不知是哪一对 | 可理解 |
| 状态卡无语义 | 「最近巩固/待确认冲突」是纯 div，不可聚焦、无 heading 层级 | 可操作 |
| 弹层焦点管理 | 记忆库 sheet 开时不移焦、无 focus trap、关闭不还焦 | 可操作 |
| 图表无替代 | ego 关系图 SVG 无可访问名称与数据摘要 | 可感知 |
| 对比度未审计 | 三级灰字 11px 在浅色主题下疑似低于 4.5:1 | 可感知 |

## 方案（分四小项，可分别认领）

1. **aria-live 网络**（新手友好）：保存/失败/刷新结果包一层 `aria-live="polite"`；错误用 `role="alert"`
2. **状态卡语义化**（新手友好）：状态卡改 `role`/heading 结构，冲突卡可聚焦可回车直达
3. **逐项操作标注**：冲突按钮 aria-label 带上对应记忆标题；弹层焦点管理（开时移焦、trap、关闭还焦）
4. **图表摘要 + 对比度审计**：ego 图加 aria-label 与文本摘要；对比度依赖宿主主题变量，需与宿主侧联调

## 验收

- 读屏（NVDA/VoiceOver 任一）完成：保存一条记忆、裁决一个冲突、浏览详情抽屉，全程无「哑」反馈
- 全键盘可完成上述流程

title: Accessibility: modals and status bar lack ARIA
body:
## Problem

- The 5 modals in `templates/game.html` (`#newgame-modal`, `#stats-modal`, `#deadlock-modal`, `#daily-modal`, `#profile-modal`) are plain `<div>`s with no `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, or `aria-labelledby` pointing at each modal's own `<h2>`.
- `#status-text` is a de-facto live region in practice (`ui-dom.js` writes messages like "No moves left", "Failed to load statistics" there) but has no `aria-live`.
- Icon/emoji-only buttons have no text alternative: `#btn-deadlock-shuffle`/`#btn-deadlock-replay`/`#btn-deadlock-giveup`, and the language picker buttons (`🌐 UA`/`🌐 EN`).

## Why it matters

A screen reader user gets no indication a modal opened, can't tell what the modal is about, doesn't hear status updates, and hears nothing useful for emoji-only buttons.

## Suggested approach

- Add `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"` + `aria-labelledby="<the modal's h2 id>"` to each of the 5 modals.
- Add `aria-live="polite"` to `#status-text`.
- Add `aria-label` to the emoji-only buttons (the board-thumbnail buttons already do this correctly — same pattern).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each modal announces itself and its title when opened via a screen reader.
- Status-bar text changes are announced.
- Every icon-only button has an accessible name.

title: fix(media): editing a caption swallows the next click on Move up/down, Make cover or Delete; focus drops to body after a move
body:
Found in exploratory testing against https://scadbuddy.internal.nullreference.io (main, `sha-30adee1`) with Playwright, 2026-10-04.

## What happens
In the Media dialog (Customize → Media), type a caption and then click Move up, Move down, Make cover or Delete on any row. The caption is saved, but the click does nothing. You have to click the button a second time.

I saw this 3 times out of 3 on a template with 4 items (`qa-epic15-widgets`, now deleted). Each time I typed into the first row's Caption and clicked that row's **Move down**:
- with Playwright `locator.click()`, twice: `GET /models/{slug}` afterwards showed the caption saved (`cap0`, then `cap1`) and the order **unchanged**;
- with a real mouse click at the button's centre: the same result (`cap1X` saved, order unchanged).

Without a caption edit first, the same Move up and Make cover buttons work on the first click.

A second problem has the same cause. After Move up, Move down or Make cover, keyboard focus drops to `<body>` (`document.activeElement` was BODY after each of them). A keyboard user who moves an item has to Tab back into the dialog from the top.

## Repro
1. Open any template of mine → **Media**, with at least 2 items.
2. Click into a row's Caption field and type something.
3. Click that row's **Move down** (or Delete, Make cover).
4. The caption is saved, but the row has not moved and no delete confirmation appears.

## Cause
`frontend/src/components/media/MediaManager.tsx`:
- The caption is saved `onBlur` (line 283), through `write()`, which calls `setBusy(true)` (line 86).
- Every row action is `disabled={locked}`, where `locked = busy || …` (line 78; the buttons at lines 266, 299, 320, 327, 337, 345 and 355).
- On mousedown the caption field blurs, the PATCH starts, React re-renders and the button under the pointer is disabled. The `click` that follows is dropped.
- For the same reason, the button that has focus is disabled while its own write runs, and the browser moves focus to `<body>`.

## Expected
- A click on a row action after editing a caption does what it says. For example, the action could queue behind the caption save, as uploads already do with `queue`, rather than being dropped.
- Focus stays on the button that was pressed, or on the moved item's row.

## Scope

Finish the accessibility pass with one CallAnnouncer, caption sizes, contrast and keyboard/focus behavior. Rewrite Commander UI/Voice-mode documentation and the Voice listening-bubble documentation to match the redesign.

## Files involved

- `src/renderer/src/components/commander/CallAnnouncer.tsx (proposed)`
- `src/renderer/src/components/commander/ (stage, captions, toolbar, action cards, PiP, sessions drawer, transcript and tests)`

- [ ] Provide S/M/L caption sizes, preserve access to complete caption text and default according to D9. The transcript is a screen-reader log.

M (~200–600 lines including tests).

Needs batches 2–6. No provider decision required. Validate the complete full-view/PiP flow against the epic’s state table and wireframes.

title: Realtime closed captions generation
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Resonite has a diverse community. People come from various cultures, languages and sometimes disabilities (e.g. hard of hearing). This can make communication difficult sometimes.

While there's a number of community made tools for this (mute helper, self-made transcription tools) a more built-in solution that can process users voices individually (e.g. to prevent multiple people talking at the same time confusing a single audio stream).

### Describe the solution you'd like

Implement a system that can perform live closed caption generation for user voices in-game and display them next to the user in UI (exposing them as data feed so users can also make custom UI's). The system will process voices of the nearby users automatically.

The solution will use the Whisper model:
- It's fully free and open source
- It can be self hosted
- It supports multiple languages and has generally good accuracy
- Using this library as wrapper: https://github.com/sandrohanea/echosharp

The processing server will be free and open source as well. This will allow:
- Anyone to host this on their own hardware, making this accessible to everyone
    - Before models like Whisper, I was looking at online services like Azure Speech Service
    - Those online models would end up being very expensive (paying > $1 for each hour of transcribed audio), which would require us to pay-gate this feature, which would be pretty bad for accessibility
    - We might offer a cloud-hosted version of this for a fee as well (we would not be able to host this for free ourselves due to compute costs), but this will never come at the cost of ability to self host
- Choose which models to use
- Add support for additional models & features and provide bug fixes by community
- Use the project outside of Resonite, improving accessibility in other projects as well

There are also some other considerations:
- The system will only process voices that the user would currently hear
     - Audio of users in whisper bubbles that the user is not inside of will not be processed at all
     - Audio of users whose audio output is currently disabled or muted will not be processed either
          - This will prevent private conversations in games like Blood On The Clocktower from leaking
- Users will be able to also run "self-transcribe" on their end, which would save processing for other users in the session
     - Similarly a headless server can run the transcription for users in the session too - however this could get heavy with lots of users and would require a lot of compute
- The processing service will announce itself on local network, making it easy for Resonite to automatically pick it up without need for manual configuration
- Multiple processing services can be ran on the local network to increase the transcription capacity - the system will spread the workload across them automatically depending on their load
- While the Whisper model is made by OpenAI, it is not a generative AI model, but a speech recognition one
     - The improvements to accessibility are also important
     - Making the processing service open source and easy to self-host should also make it everyone's choice whether to use this model or not (it will not be shipped with Resonite itself, but be a separate add-on to download) and ensure that this is not gated behind a paywall
- The transcribed audio can also then be ran through a translation service (either local or API) to allow for easy multi-lingual communication
    - I haven't looked into potential solutions for this yet. Whisper can do some translation itself, but I'm not sure how good it is at this
    - This can be both local models for translation or online services
- The service can also be used to transcribe voice messages - though this is a stretch goal right now

### Describe alternatives you've considered

Leaving this to mods and community. However there's a few issues with thi

title: An author's alternative text is not visible when the image is shown
body: Found while checking #14 (PR #16) on the iPDF flyer from #12, in the tagged reading. ## What happens `Figure` in `lib/reader/renderer.tsx` decides what is drawn and what goes in `alt`: | Figure | Text on screen | `` | |---|---|---| | Author alt, image shown | **none** | the author's text, e.g. 「アイコン：PDF」 | | Author alt, no image (too small to crop) | 「画像: 図：i」 | (no image) | | No alt, or text written by an AI or by the word processor | the notice | empty, so it is not read twice | The rule is deliberate. Text the document supplied behaves like alternative text always has: announced, not drawn. Text this tool produced is drawn, so that it can be checked by looking. In the flyer, the PDF icon after 「あなたが作った」 and the crying eye after 「ひとがいます」 have author alt text. It is in `alt`, and VoiceOver reads it (the reporter of #12 confirmed this). Nothing is drawn, and nothing appears when the Reader is printed. ## Why it matters 1. **What the author wrote cannot be confirmed by looking.** Reading it takes a screen reader or the developer tools. Checking alternative text is one of the main uses of this Reader (see #1 and #12), and for someone doing that on screen this is the one piece they cannot see. 2. **The same author text is shown in one case and hidden in the other.** With an image, it is hidden. Without one (a too-small figure), it is drawn as 「画像: 図：i」. 3. **"No notice means the author gave alt text" is a convention nothing on screen states.** From the screen alone, there is no way to tell it apart from a figure whose notice failed to render. ## Options - **A. Always draw the author's alt text** under the image, with `alt=""` so it is not read twice. The same prefix scheme as the other notices applies; 「画像: …」 already says the text is the document's own. - **B. A setting to show alternative text on screen**, off by default, keeping the current behaviour for screen reader users who do not want every image described twice in reading order. - **C. Keep it in `alt` and show it on demand**, for example on hover or focus. This is weaker for print and for anyone not using a pointer. ## To decide - Which of A, B or C. A and B change what a screen reader hears: with A, the text moves from the image to a paragraph after it. - How an author's `alt=""` (decorative) is shown, which today is 「装飾的な画像です。内容はありません。」 only when there is no image. - Whether print should always include the text, whatever the on-screen choice. ## Related - #14 / PR #16: the notices for figures without alt text. - #15: the size threshold. It decides which figures fall in the "no image" row above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
