title: Accessibility pass (PRD §18)
body:
Part of #15
Blocked by: #26, #29

## What to build

Check and fix the §18 requirements across the built views.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contrast: `text-primary`/`text-secondary` ≥ 4.5:1 on `bg-deep`/`bg-panel`; `text-dim` only on non-essential captions (≥ 3:1); checked by a script against the Theme
- [ ] No state is shown by colour alone (letters, labels, glyphs, badges)
- [ ] Logical focus order (strip top → bottom, strips left → right); the focus ring is always visible
- [ ] Controls expose role, name and value text to screen readers (JUCE accessibility handlers)
- [ ] UI scale 80–200 %; hit targets ≥ 16 px
- [ ] Reduce motion: peaks fall instantly, queued clips don't blink

Source: `PRD.md` v1.0, `design/design.pen`.

## Spec (moved from PRD)

Moved verbatim from `PRD.md` v1.1 on 2026-09-29. This section is now the source of truth for it; the PRD keeps only the heading with a pointer here.

## 18. Accessibility

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Contrast | Text ≥ 4.5 : 1 against its surface for `text-primary` and `text-secondary` on `bg-deep`/`bg-panel`; `text-dim` limited to non-essential captions (≥ 3 : 1). |
| Colour independence | State is never colour-only: M/S/● letters, `PRE/POST` labels, `Ø` glyph, `OVERRIDDEN` text, badges carry words. |
| Keyboard | Every control focusable in logical order (strip top → bottom, strips left → right); `focus-ring` always visible; arrow keys adjust focused continuous controls. |
| Screen reader | Controls expose role, name and value text (e.g. "Vocal, Send B, 25 %, pre-fader, pan left 30, polarity inverted"). |
| Scaling | UI scale 80–200 % (min text 7.5 px at 100 % → 9 px at 120 % default recommended on non-retina). |
| Motion | Meter/animation respects "reduce motion" (peak falls instantly, no blinking queued clips — use outline instead). |
| Hit targets | Minimum 16 × 16 px (TrackBtn); 20 px preferred. |
| Plug-in windows | Host chrome (title bar, toolbar, footer) is fully keyboard and screen-reader accessible even when the vendor UI isn't. `Esc` returns focus from the plug-in to the host. Opening a window on insert moves focus to it and announces "*Plug-in* window opened". |
| Native vs plug-in | The difference isn't colour-only: plug-ins always carry the plug icon, vendor and format text. |
| Sidechain | Links are announced with direction, e.g. "Compressor, sidechain from Drums, Kick, pre-FX". The `key-round` icon and `SC ←/→` text accompany the teal colour. Disabled picker rows expose their reason ("self", "feedback loop"). |

## Correction request  

The AV Annotations TSG would like to add the proposed [provides property](https://github.com/IIIF/api/issues/2308) to this recipe, allowing the IIIF client to distinguish between captions (original language, needed for accessibility) and subtitles (translations from original language). In the recipe, the first file would be labeled with `provides='openCaptions'` and the second `provides='subtitles'`. Note that the term `subtitles` is not included in the original vocabulary for the `provides` property, and this is a demonstration of the use case for adding it.

Common usage (across IU and Europeana) when there are multiple languages for caption and subtitle files is to use multiple `supplementing` annotations, rather than a `choice` construct within a single annotation. Could we separate the `choice` construct into 2 annotations, each with its own `provides` property?

title: Investigate allowing headings within table captions
body:
## What

Investigate whether allowing headings within table captions may make it easier for users to understand the hierarchy of information on a page or to navigate the page.

## Why

Captions are styled similarly to headings, but are not headings so do not show up in headings lists and are not included when navigating using headings in screen readers.

The [content model for the `caption` element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#the-caption-element) allows for any flow content, which includes headings, so it's a valid thing to do according to the HTML spec.

## Assumptions

Including a heading within the caption does not affect the role of either the caption or the heading, nor how they are communicated to users of assistive technologies.

## Timebox

TBC

## Who is working on this?

Spike lead: TBC

Spike buddy: TBC

## Questions to answer

- Is there any established best practise around this?
- Do users expect to see table captions included in the list of headings, or to expect them to act as headings e.g. for navigation?
- In which scenarios does it make sense to put a heading in a caption, if any?
- What changes do we need to make to allow headings in captions?

## Done when

- [ ] Questions have been answered or we have a clearer idea of how to get to our goal
- [ ] Findings have been reviewed and agreed with at least one other person
- [ ] Findings have been shared, e.g: via a write-up on the ticket, at a show & tell or team meeting

title: Captions Cut Off in Fullscreen on Chrome
body: ### Subject of the issue/enhancement/features Some users have reported that captions (subtitles) get cut off or overlap the video controls when watching videos in fullscreen mode on Chrome. - This issue only happens in fullscreen on some versions of Chrome. - It works fine in Firefox and in normal (non-fullscreen) mode. - The problem seems to happen when captions have two lines, and the second line drops too low and gets hidden behind the player bar. MediaElement.js uses native browser caption rendering by default (renderCaptionsNatively: true). In Chrome, native captions are rendered by the browser itself, and: - Cannot be styled via regular CSS (line-height, bottom, etc.) - May be influenced by the user's system caption settings - In fullscreen, Chrome often repositions captions downward, and the second line may get tucked underneath the media player bar. Meanwhile, Firefox appears to render native captions differently (more predictably), or positions them upward to stay within bounds of the video frame. ### Your environment * FW v5.45.2 * Media v7.0.0 * Chrome 140.0.7339.128 * Window & MacOS ### Steps to reproduce Using the following configuration above, add a multi-line caption to a video and play in Chrome fullscreen. ### Temporary Fixes To reduce the impact of the issue: 1. Smaller Caption Text in Fullscreen - We've reduced the caption font size when a video goes fullscreen. This makes it less likely that the second line will get cut off. But understand this isn't a good long-term solution. 2. Auto-Hide the Player Bar - Captions don't get blocked. ### Possible Long-term fixes - Evaluate the mediaelement.js library to see if any settings exist - Possibly disable native caption rendering by browsers. Instead apply our own styles. - Manually detect fullscreen / Chrome and attempt to override styles programmatically. ### Screenshots (if you can) Chrome fullscreen CC Text rendering

title: Code chunk figures with fig-pos='H' produce broken PDF tag structure with pdf-standard: ua-2
body:
## Summary

When a figure uses `\begin{figure}[H]` (from LaTeX's `float` package), lualatex's PDF tagging system produces broken tag structure: `/Caption` and `/Figure` appear as direct children of `/Document` instead of being properly nested. This causes PDF/UA-2 validation failure: `<Document> shall not contain <Caption>`.

This affects multiple code paths that inject `[H]`:

1. **Code chunk figures** — both knitr and Jupyter automatically inject `fig-pos='H'` when code is echoed
2. **Non-cross-referenceable captioned images** — `pandoc3_figure.lua` injects `[H]` on figures without `#fig-` labels
3. **Panel layouts** — `quarto-post/latex.lua` forces `[H]` on figures inside panels

Cross-referenceable static images (`[image]{#fig-label}`) were not affected only because they happen to not get `[H]` injected — not because of any structural difference in the LaTeX output.

## Reproducer

````qmd
---
title: "Code chunk figure tag structure"
lang: en
format:
  pdf:
    pdf-standard: ua-2
---

```{r}
#| label: fig-mpg-by-weight
#| fig-cap: "MPG vs weight by cylinder count"
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

See @fig-mpg-by-weight.
````

**Expected:** verapdf validation passes.
**Actual:** verapdf reports `<Document> shall not contain <Caption>`.

## Root cause

The `[H]` specifier (from LaTeX's `float` package) redefines the figure environment in a way that's incompatible with lualatex's PDF tagging system. Standard LaTeX placement specifiers use the native float mechanism, which the tagging system handles correctly.

The LaTeX output is structurally identical with and without `[H]` — both produce `\begin{figure}...\caption{...}\end{figure}`. The difference is entirely in how lualatex's tagging system processes the float internally.

### Where `[H]` is injected

- **Knitr**: `src/resources/rmd/hooks.R:661-667` — sets `fig-pos='H'` when `echo=TRUE`, no user `fig-pos`, no layout options, and LaTeX output
- **Jupyter**: `src/core/jupyter/jupyter.ts:1625-1631` — same logic
- **Non-cross-referenceable figures**: `src/resources/filters/layout/pandoc3_figure.lua:126-132` — sets `fig-pos='H'` on figures with empty identifier
- **Panel layouts**: `src/resources/filters/quarto-post/latex.lua` — forces `[H]` on floats inside panels

### Empirical testing of placement specifiers

Tested each placement specifier with `pdf-standard: ua-2` and verapdf validation:

| Specifier | verapdf result |
|-----------|---------------|
| (none) | **PASSED** |
| `[h]` | **PASSED** |
| `[htbp]` | **PASSED** |
| `[H]` | **FAILED** — `<Document> shall not contain <Caption>` |

Only `[H]` (from the `float` package) breaks tagging. All standard LaTeX specifiers work correctly.

## Proposed fix

When PDF tagging is active (`pdf-standard` includes a standard that requires tagging, like `ua-2`), replace `fig-pos='H'` with `fig-pos='h'` across all injection points. `[h]` is the closest semantic equivalent to `[H]` ("place here") without the `float` package's incompatible reimplementation.

## Workaround

Setting `echo: false` on code chunks avoids the `[H]` injection for that specific case, since the placement logic only triggers when code is echoed.

title: Wide tables give no sign that they scroll, so they read as truncated
body:
## Capability
A table that is wider than its container looks scrollable, so a reader tries to scroll it instead of concluding the site is broken.

## Why this exists
`src/styles/global.css:308` is the whole rule: `.tableview-scroll { overflow-x: auto; margin-top: 0.9rem; }`. There is no fade, no shadow, no persistent scrollbar and no text hint. On the platforms this site is read on, overlay scrollbars are hidden until a scroll is already in progress, so a wide table presents as a table with its right-hand columns simply missing.

Measured on the deployed site during the browser review, 2026-08-24:

- **Economy**, desktop 1440x900: the table is 1216px inside a 736px wrapper. Columns 4 through 7 are off-screen with nothing indicating they exist.
- **Government §11**, mobile 390x844: cells extend to `x=1102` inside a 350px wrapper, and the figure caption is cut at the viewport edge. The review's note was that it "reads as broken rather than scrollable".

The consequence is specific to this site. Every chart carries a "View as table" disclosure because that table is the non-visual and non-graphical equivalent of the chart — it is what discharges the shared done contract of section issues #2 through #15. A reader who cannot tell that four of seven columns exist has not been given that equivalent; they have been given a truncated one they have no reason to doubt.

Filed separately per #30's definition of done.

## Scope
- A visible affordance on any horizontal scroll container whose content overflows: a directional fade or shadow at the overflowing edge, or a persistent scrollbar, or both.
- The affordance appears **only when the content actually overflows**, and disappears when it does not — it is viewport-dependent, so this is a runtime condition rather than a static style.
- Applies to `.tableview-scroll` (`src/components/islands/TableView.tsx:30`) and to the §11 by-state table, which `src/pages/government/index.astro` renders as plain markup outside `TableView` (see `docs/parked-findings.md`).

Out of scope: making the tables narrow enough not to overflow, and the keyboard reachability of the scroll container, which is #71.

## Edge cases
- The affordance must indicate **which** edge overflows and update as the reader scrolls, or a fade on the right will still be showing when the reader has already reached the end.
- A fade drawn over the table's rightmost column must not obscure a value. Prefer an affordance outside the content box, or one narrow enough to sit in the cell padding.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` if the affordance animates in or out (`src/styles/global.css:612-619` has the existing block).
- The page background is `--ground` and the panel is `--panel`; a fade must be drawn against whichever the table actually sits on, or it will show as a grey band on the wrong one.
- With JavaScript off, the `<details>` still opens (it is native — `src/components/islands/TableView.tsx:4`) and the table still overflows. A JS-driven affordance leaves the JS-off reader exactly where they are today; say whether that is accepted or whether the affordance must be CSS-only.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Every horizontal scroll container that overflows shows an affordance indicating there is more content, on both routes where this was observed and anywhere else it occurs.
- [ ] A container that does not overflow shows no affordance.
- [ ] The affordance tracks scroll position and clears at the end of travel.
- [ ] No value in the table is obscured by it.
- [ ] Stated and recorded whether the JS-off case is covered.
- [ ] `npx astro check` clean; `npm run build` clean; `cd pipeline && uv run pytest` green.

## Verification
- In a browser at 1440x900 on `/economy`, open a "View as table", assert the affordance is present, scroll to the far right, assert it clears.
- At 1440x900 on a table that fits, assert no affordance is rendered.
- Repeat both at 390x844 on `/government` §11.

## Dependencies
None.

title: Meaningful Pan & Zoom (and Feature navigation)
body:
> [!NOTE] > A developer reached out to me and wrote I'm trying to decide on an open-source map library and one of my priorities is accessibility. Would you be willing to provide some advice regarding the state of accessibility with these mapping libraries?. > > Not only do _all_ of the [libraries fail to implement a basic UI in an accessible manner](https://github.com/Malvoz/web-maps-wcag-evaluation) (i.e. https://github.com/Maps4HTML/Web-Map-Custom-Element/issues/247), but panning and zooming is for the most part meaningless to non-visual users. Can pan and zoom (and map navigation as a whole) be made useful and meaningful, to everyone? ## The problems 1. **Panning & zooming is not meaningful to users of assistive technology** - There is no feedback provided to the user during/after pan and zoom, so these actions have no meaning to a non-visual user. - Panning and zooming has (mostly) no effect on the visibility/focusability of elements, which leads to the next problem: 2. **Navigating only features of interest** - It's not possible to only navigate features currently in view (whether "currently in view" is limited to a square in the center of the map or the visible content of the map viewer itself). Currently, if only 1 out of 100 focusable elements are in view there are still 100 elements in the tab order. ## Potential solution(s) (These solution parts are highly inspired by the [Google Maps site](https://www.google.com/maps)'s "[Accessibility Mode](https://support.google.com/maps/answer/6396990?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en)" and [Esri's a11y-map](https://github.com/Esri/a11y-map), and rely on [`role=application`](https://github.com/Maps4HTML/Web-Map-Custom-Element/pull/467) such that screen reader users can pan using arrow keys as well). 1. **The direction in which the user is panning should be announced** - _Example:_ pressing → should announce Moving East (although cardinal directions are not relevant in [_drawings or schematics without geographic coordinates_](https://maps4html.org/HTML-Map-Element-UseCases-Requirements/#use-case-technical-drawings)). - _Why?_ This would allow non-visual users to learn in which direction a feature is located in relation to others. - _How?_ A (potentially [sr-only](https://webaim.org/techniques/css/invisiblecontent/#offscreen)) ARIA [Live Region](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/ARIA_Live_Regions) element (e.g. [`role="status"`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#status) with [`aria-atomic="true"`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-atomic)):

```html Moving East. ``` 2. **The zoom level should be announced** (https://github.com/Maps4HTML/Web-Map-Custom-Element/issues/664) - _Example:_ pressing + (or Enter/Space when the Zoom In control has focus) should announce e.g. Zoom level 10. - _Why?_ This would allow non-visual users to learn how much to zoom in/out to reach a certain feature (but also the initial zoom level). - _How?_ A (potentially sr-only) ARIA Live Region element:

```html Zoom level: 10. ``` 3. **Min/max zoom & pan should be announced when reached** - _Example:_ pressing - (or Enter/Space when the Zoom Out control has focus) and reaching the minimum zoom level should announce e.g. Minimum zoom level reached: zoom out disabled. - _Why?_ This would allow non-visual users to learn that they've reached the min/max zoom level and/or bounds of the map. - _How?_ A (potentially sr-only) Live

title: The Wall does not survive larger text
body:
## What happens

The Wall is sized in rem, with a few constants in px. Measured by arithmetic on the v2 build at 1280 x 800:

- At 130 percent text size the navigation rail needs more than the screen's height, so Add event is pushed off the screen, and Month shows only counts.
- At 200 percent a day column on Home is 28 px wide, Month's dates clip, and the Profile chips collapse to nothing.
- `MIN_TARGET_PX = 48` and `GRID_PADDING_PX = 24` in `src/components/FiveDayCalendar.tsx:39-40` are px while the blocks are `min-h-12` (rem), so as soon as text passes 100 percent, blocks are drawn taller than they are laned for and events overlap.

Whether Fully Kiosk Browser applies Android's font size as text zoom or page zoom has not been checked on the tablet.

## Suggested fix

Compute the 48 px minimum from the measured rem, as `MonthGrid` does. Cap the rails (for example `min(22rem, 27vw)`). Let the Profile chips wrap. Check the tablet at its largest font setting.

Found in the accessibility audit of the v2 build. Filed for triage; nothing here blocks the release. The look itself is being redone under the next spec; this is the engineering side.

title: Feature request: Text Size in settings, and in comments of eg. Youtube
body:
### Use Cases

This is because it is impossible to Zoom in the Grayjay App with two finger gesture, as in Chrome browser, ot indeed most other Android Apps. There are zero options to set text size in either the App itself, or for any of the plugins either. This is a major oversight, and frankly I blame the developers for no doubt composing these Apps and Plugins on very large display screens where this issue isn't apparent. Just try to read the text in "settings" on an ordinary tiny mobile phone screen, that cannot be zoomed with two finger gesture. Quite apart from the tiny size, the text is in gray on black in the Dark mode, and this makes readability even worse. 

Again, it's impossible to copy and paste ANY text from the comments of ANY plugin either (so as to paste into a notepad or email) and this is another oversight as well. Please give consideration to allow two finger zoom for the app in Android permissions, as there is no extant setting to do so, anywhere in the App, or in its Android settings either.

### Proposal

title: UI font-size / elements too small
body:
It's been bothering me for years. The content of the UI is unreadable small, especially during a work day when your eyes become tired, Tine renders unusable. I don't know how you manage it. I personally zoom in a lot; every browser supports that,(I know the key shortcut and do it automatically. Now and then, however, zoomed elements break the UI and I "compensate" this by manual zoom (but that's only me).  

Today I have talked to someone, introducing Tine. Because it wasn't my device, everything was in default - way too small. I realized then how small it really is! The showcase was over, though ("looks like 90s..."). 

Just to clear the dimension: 

- Elements become distinguishable with a **minimum zoom of 133 %** the earliest. On a standard notebook / desktop display without zoom, text is literally not readable. Meaning you are guessing the letters not reading due to "lost" pixels. 
- SVG images start to appear clean only with zoom, the displays I tested it needs **at least 150 %**. 
- Standard font-sizes in the panels, including specially designed contents like calendar sheets, also render clean at 150 % the earliest. 
- For "working content" like the Text of emails I would prefer even 200% zoom. This may not be suitable as a global setting. However, to really work with text without eye tiredness it would be preferable. 

I am not a designer. But you can read all over the web that typically **regular text is not smaller than 16px** (Tine: 11px standard elements), 11px is tolerated only for additional illustration like Button description or "badges". I also realize that this changed over time as displays got higher resolution. However, today I would call it a bug (I got it mirrored today by someone "neutral")

As a quick relieve: I do not see any harm in adjusting everything by 133 %. Do you? 

Because of Tine I had look into OnlyOffice - they do it very right UI wise...

title: Complete the accessibility audit
body:
## Outcome

Both production windows satisfy the defined keyboard, focus, contrast, scaling, announcement, and reduced-motion requirements.

## Scope

- Audit every shared component and complete operator/public flow with automated and manual checks.
- Verify keyboard-only operation, focus order/restoration, dialogs, live regions, zoom, projector readability, and high-contrast theme.
- Correct issues without weakening the component or token contracts.
- Record remaining platform-specific limitations explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria

- The visible outcome is exercised through the real operator or public renderer as applicable.
- State changes are acknowledged only from committed persistence snapshots; failures preserve the last committed state.
- Existing Electron sandbox, context-isolation, preload, IPC, offline-asset, and persistence guarantees remain intact.
- Strict RED → GREEN → REFACTOR evidence and proportionate automated tests are required.
- Relevant accessibility, reduced-motion, restart/reopen, and integrated Electron smoke evidence is recorded.

## Dependencies

Core operator/public and game flows are complete.

## Delivery budget

180–320 changed lines. A PR reaching 800 authored changed lines is not acceptable and must be split. Generated build output is excluded from authored scope and remains outside commits.

## Non-goals

No card/ticket generation, import, registration, distribution, claimant identity, or automated line/bingo validation. No second-line prize. No user-facing export, backup, or restore unless this issue explicitly states otherwise.

## Delivery status (2026-09-30)

- Delivered foundations: semantic token/contrast contracts (#74/#85), automated component accessibility coverage and Storybook verification (#93/#95), keyboard/focus contracts for existing operator forms and board, and responsive public presentation (#98).
- Remaining: the dedicated end-to-end audit of both production windows, including complete award/final/archive flows once implemented, keyboard-only navigation, focus restoration, announcements, zoom/projector readability, reduced motion and recorded manual/platform limitations.
- Automated axe/Storybook passes do not by themselves complete this audit. Keep this issue open; do not rebuild delivered foundations.

title: Set accessibility scope and roll out improvements
body:
## Summary

Set a repository-wide accessibility scope and improve RSS Dashboard incrementally, using WCAG 2.2 Level AA as a design and audit reference without claiming current conformance.

## Why

The repository has useful local expectations, but they were scattered across design and contributor docs, with conflicting legacy icon-control guidance. The plugin has no comprehensive accessibility audit, verified assistive-technology support matrix, or consistent plan for human and AI-assisted verification.

## Adopted direction

- Human accessibility is the purpose and deciding factor. AI-agent testability is an added benefit, not the primary driver.
- Apply the scope to plugin-owned UI and content across desktop, mobile, and popout contexts. Document Obsidian-host and third-party-content boundaries and verified gaps.
- Prefer semantic controls and keyboard paths. Combine automated and CDP accessibility-tree checks and screenshots with keyboard verification and targeted screen-reader checks; no automated scan alone proves conformance.
- Improve shared patterns and clear severe barriers as work proceeds. Use task impact and component reuse to guide ordering, with coverage as a risk signal. Do not require an analytics-heavy usage or coverage study first.

## Workstreams and acceptance criteria

1. Maintain the root `ACCESSIBILITY.md` as the user-facing scope, limitations, reporting path, and maintenance reference; link it from the README and contributor guidance.
2. Keep detailed implementation expectations aligned across contributor instructions, the design spec, and test guidance. Remove the `title` exception and clearly mark custom `div[role="button"]` controls as legacy during migration.
3. Improve reusable patterns and address severe or high-impact barriers incrementally across supported contexts, without waiting for an exhaustive surface inventory.
4. Record what was verified and what remains unknown. Require keyboard verification for changed interactive flows and targeted screen-reader checks for changes to names, state, focus, or dynamic announcements.
5. Use user-facing semantic controls and keyboard behavior for agent-driven tests where practical; CDP accessibility-tree inspection and screenshots supplement that path.
6. Route user reports through GitHub Issues using the existing `accessibility` label. Review the scope when supported surfaces, Obsidian requirements, standards, or testing tools change.

## Scope boundaries

This is an umbrella issue. Surface-specific fixes discovered during rollout can be tracked in focused issues. Obsidian host UI and remote article content are external dependencies; report their barriers accurately without claiming RSS Dashboard controls them.

[Issue #502](https://github.com/amatya-aditya/obsidian-rss-dashboard/issues/502) already records the accepted native-button direction and its styling spike. Continue it independently; this umbrella issue and the policy work do not block it.

## Related materials

- `ACCESSIBILITY.md`
- `docs/adr/0016-wcag-22-aa-accessibility-reference.md`
- `docs/plans/draft-20261002-accessibility-rollout.md`
- `docs/development/accessibility-research.md`

## Focused accessibility issues

This is an ongoing work-in-progress. Append focused accessibility issues to this table as they are surfaced. Keep closed issues in the table as a record of completed work. This table is an index; each linked issue holds its detailed scope, acceptance criteria, evidence, and current status.

title: Site-wide: nine more colours fail WCAG AA, on all 24 pages
body:
Found while fixing #6. Filing separately because the fix is a site-wide restyle, which does not belong inside an issue scoped to six files.

## What

#6 was scoped to the Field Notes tree. Measuring that tree surfaced failures that are **not** in the Field Notes CSS — they come from `base.css` and page-level CSS, and therefore render on all 24 pages.

Confirmed present on `/`, `/about.html`, `/services.html` and `/pt/` as well as the Field Notes pages.

| Selector | Colour | Measured | Needs | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.footer-logo` | `#6b7485` (`--gray-500`) | **3.83:1** | 4.5 | `base.css`, every page |
| footer social links | `#6b7485` | **3.83:1** | 4.5 | `base.css`, every page |
| `.footer-copy` | `#6b7485` | **3.83:1** | 4.5 | `base.css`, every page |
| `em` in body copy | `#6b7485` | **3.83:1** | 4.5 | page CSS |
| `.hero-scope` | `rgba(240,241,243,0.45)` | 4.08:1 | 4.5 | `index.html` |
| language switch `/` | `rgba(15,25,45,0.6)` | 4.21:1 | 4.5 | `base.css`, every page |
| `.tab-link.active` | `#576e20` | 4.40:1 | 4.5 | page CSS |
| language switch links | `rgba(15,25,45,0.62)` | 4.47:1 | 4.5 | `base.css`, every page |
| `.nav-quiz-link` | `rgba(15,25,45,0.62)` | 4.47:1 | 4.5 | `base.css`, every page |

The footer is the significant one: `--gray-500` at 3.83:1 is the same order of failure as the Field Notes bug, and it is on every page of the site including the legal pages.

Four of these are marginal (4.08 to 4.47), which is its own lesson — they were almost certainly picked by eye and looked fine.

## Method

Measured in a headless browser rather than by reading CSS: rgba foregrounds composited over the effective background chain, and the AA threshold selected per element from its own computed font size and weight, so large text is correctly held to 3:1 rather than 4.5:1.

## Do

- Raise `--gray-500` until the footer passes at its rendered sizes. It is a token, so check what else consumes it before changing the value — a token change is not a local change
- Fix the nav chrome: dark text on `--green-500` is only just failing, so a small darkening of the text or a slight lift of the green will clear it
- Fix `.hero-scope` and `.tab-link.active`
- Re-measure rather than assuming a value passes

## Careful

`--gray-500` is a design token. Changing it moves every element that uses it, which is the point, but it means this needs a before/after render comparison across pages, not just a contrast re-check.

## Acceptance

- [ ] No text colour anywhere on the site computes below its WCAG AA threshold
- [ ] Token changes verified not to have altered layout or unrelated components
- [ ] CHANGELOG records the token change specifically, since it is the highest-blast-radius edit

## Related

- #6 fixed the Field Notes tree only, and records these nine as knowingly deferred
- #9's contrast check should cover the whole site, not just Field Notes, or this stays invisible

## Summary

Reconcile the existing Playwright axe suite and the accessibility/testing specs around one explicit WCAG 2.1 A/AA enforcement policy.

- [ ] Run the current suite with explicit WCAG 2.1 A/AA tags and record the additional violations that would be enforced if all impacts became blocking.
- [ ] Decide from that evidence whether CI should retain serious/critical enforcement or block every WCAG 2.1 A/AA-tagged violation.
- [ ] Keep coverage of every article at desktop and mobile unless measured runtime or reliability evidence justifies a narrower representative set.
- [ ] Update the existing Playwright spec; do not add a duplicate axe-audit suite.

## Expected outcome

The implemented Playwright behavior and all three canonical specs describe one evidence-based WCAG 2.1 A/AA automation contract, with no stale references to adding coverage that already exists.

title: fix(ui): faint text, accent links and primary buttons fail WCAG AA contrast (3.1–3.9:1)
body:
Found in exploratory testing against https://scadbuddy.internal.nullreference.io (main) with Playwright, 2026-10-01.

Text contrast was computed (WCAG 2.x relative luminance) for every visible text node on `/`, `/m/qa-explore-cube` and `/settings`, in both `prefers-color-scheme` modes. Disabled controls are excluded. Three tokens fail AA for normal-size text (4.5:1); all the affected text is 11–14px.

| Token pair | Theme | Ratio | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--sb-faint` #808d9d on surface #ffffff | light | **3.38** | "OpenSCAD customizer", "Built-in template — read-only", card "Updated 2 minutes ago" / "From httpbin.org", Customize "Defaults", breadcrumb "/" |
| `--sb-faint` #808d9d on bg #f4f6f9 | light | **3.12** | tag counts (35, 26…), "H2C · 12.99 × 12.60 in plate" |
| `--sb-faint` #5d6a7c on surface #131822 | dark | **3.23** | same elements |
| `--sb-faint` #5d6a7c on bg #0b0e13 | dark | **3.51** | tag counts, plate-size badge |
| `--sb-accent` #b96f05 on #ffffff, as **text** | light | **3.93** | Settings "Reset to deployment value" (11px), card "Update available" (11px), "Temporal UI ↗", repository links |
| `--sb-accent-ink` #fff8ec on `--sb-accent` #b96f05 | light | **3.73** | every primary button: Add model, Generate, Print in dialogs (14px) |

Dark mode's accent pair (#1a1204 on #f2a93b) and `--sb-muted` in both themes pass.

## Expected
AA (4.5:1) for these sizes. For example, light `--sb-faint` #646f7f or darker (about 4.6 on #f4f6f9), dark `--sb-faint` around #7a8799 (about 4.9 on #131822), and a darker light-mode accent for text and button fills (e.g. #9a5c04 gives about 5.0 against white and against #fff8ec). body:
The [`<VersionSelector>`](https://github.com/npmx-dev/npmx.dev/blob/3cf7fef97cef6be97e8f9ace628c88757a1b0c84/app/components/VersionSelector.vue) component [used in the package code page](https://github.com/npmx-dev/npmx.dev/blob/3cf7fef97cef6be97e8f9ace628c88757a1b0c84/app/pages/package-code/%5B...path%5D.vue#L322-L330) is not accessible for screen readers.

The root of the problem is that [ARIA role `option`](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#option) shouldn’t nest interactive content (or really any semantic content). Its children are expected to be [presentational](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#childrenArePresentational).

The current incorrect structure is like this:

- `role=listbox`
  - `role=option`
    - `role=button`
    - `role=link`
    - (then a list of `role=option` shown when the button is `aria-expanded=true`)

ARIA doesn’t expect there to be anything past the `role=option` (i.e. the contents are meant to be used for its accessible name).

On Windows 11, NVDA (in Firefox and Edge) is able to focus the expand/collapse button and link and even trigger the buttons, however, it cannot trigger the link.

On macOS and iOS, VoiceOver both do not go further than the `role=option` widgets (and do nothing when activated).

**We will need different semantics** which I can research. I suspect it might be a multi-level list of expand/collapse buttons + links that is focus trapped while it’s open. A treeview could be another option, but that has some significant complexity to it and shouldn’t be used lightly. The README table of contents is also using `role=listbox` when it probably shouldn’t, so it would be good to unify on an approach (even if the components are styled different).

I could add some screen caps when I get a change to better demonstrate the issue.

title: a11y(web): async loading states (profile, invoice detail, marketplace, dashboard form) are not announced to screen readers
body:
## Summary
Only a handful of components expose a live region (`grep -rn 'role="status"\|aria-busy' apps/web/app apps/web/components` finds `TopStatusBar`, `InvoiceTable`, `InvoiceStatus` and `VerificationBadge` only). Several route-level loading states render purely visual text/spinners, so a screen-reader user hears nothing while data loads and nothing when it arrives:

- `apps/web/app/profile/page.tsx`: "Syncing credential ledger..." with an `animate-ping` dot in a plain `div`
- `apps/web/app/invoice/[invoiceId]/InvoiceDetailClient.tsx` (~line 108): the loading block is `<div className="... animate-pulse uppercase">`
- `apps/web/app/marketplace/page.tsx`: the "Syncing..." label next to the results heading, and the "Available Invoices (N)" count that changes when filters change
- `apps/web/app/dashboard/page.tsx`: the `InvoiceForm` dynamic-import fallback is a bare CSS spinner with no text
- `components/shared/SkeletonLoader.tsx` skeleton wrappers have no `aria-busy`/label, and the `loading.tsx` route files render only skeletons

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Loading messages use `role="status"` (polite) with meaningful text, and spinners get visually-hidden text such as "Loading invoice form"
- [ ] Skeleton containers set `aria-busy="true"` and an `aria-label`/sr-only description ("Loading invoices") and are removed/updated when content mounts
- [ ] The marketplace result count sits in a polite live region so filter changes are announced
- [ ] Add tests asserting the `status` role on each of the above states

## Tech Stack
Next.js, `apps/web/app/profile/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/invoice/[invoiceId]/InvoiceDetailClient.tsx`, `apps/web/app/marketplace/page.tsx`, `apps/web/components/shared/SkeletonLoader.tsx`

title: ai: Accessibility-first Cooking Navigator modes (screen reader, motor, cognitive, low vision)
body:
## Parent
Part of Wave 5 epic #358.

## Problem
AI cooking products often optimize for flashy vision/voice demos while excluding users who benefit most from structured assistance. Seasoned has general a11y backlog (#330 theme, #329 targets, #323 focus traps) but **cook execution** needs a dedicated accessibility mode suite so AI step coaching is usable with screen readers, switch controls, large type, reduced motion, and cognitive plain-language.

## Trend → best practice
- Inclusive design is table stakes for mainstream consumer apps and increasingly expected in health-adjacent coaching.
- Progressive disclosure (#355) should **pair** with cognitive load modes, not only chef skill.
- Voice agent (# voice child) must expose the same capabilities via keyboard/SR.

## Goals
1. **Screen reader mode**: step regions with live regions for timer ticks (polite), actionable names (“Step 3 of 12: Simmer sauce, button”).
2. **Low vision**: large type scale (// 1.4), high contrast cook chrome, invert-safe images, avoid color-only doneness cues (ties #343).
3. **Motor**: full keyboard; 44px targets (#329); optional dwell/switch access documentation; prevent accidental gesture back.
4. **Cognitive**: plain-language step alternate (`step.simple_text`) from generate/enrich; one-action-per-screen option; reduced concurrent timers display.
5. Settings: `a11y_cook_profile` stored in culinary profile or local device preferences.

## Non-goals
- Certifying full WCAG for entire app in this issue (Navigator critical path only).
- Replacing professional occupational therapy tools.

## User stories
- As a VoiceOver user, I complete a pasta recipe using rotor and announcements when timers end.
- As a user with low vision, I cook with large type and hear steps without relying on pale glassmorphism.
- As a user with ADHD, one-step focus mode hides the full list until I request it.

## Technical approach
- Audit `CookingNavigator.jsx` + timer components; fix roles/labels first.
- Generation enrichment field `instructions[].accessibility` optional via worker flag.
- Prefer CSS tokens over one-off styles; respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-contrast`.
- Flag `a11y_cook_v1`.
- Add axe/playwright a11y checks for Navigator route.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Critical path WCAG 2.2 AA issues = 0 on Navigator with axe (flag build).
- [ ] Timer completion announced once; focus not stolen mid-type.
- [ ] All gestures have button equivalents.
- [ ] Plain-language toggle works online; falls back to original text offline.
- [ ] Documented screen reader test script in docs or issue checklist.
- [ ] No regression to allergen banners (must remain readable and announced).

## Success metrics
- Moderated study task success ≥ parity with non-a11y baseline (n≥8).
- Zero Sev-1 a11y bugs open >14d on Navigator after ship.
- Adoption: ≥5% of users enable an a11y cook setting within 60d (discovery sanity).

## Dependencies
- #329, #323, #330, #355 skill-adaptive text, voice agent child, offline package must include `simple_text` when present.

## References
- Internal UI a11y issues #329 #323 #330
- FoodsGPT / education trend: culinary education powered by AI
- Repo: `CookingNavigator.jsx`, `MealPlanner.css`, `index.css`

title: Screen reader doesn't announce Notification
body:
### Description

In our webapp Chrome with NVDA and Firefox with NVDA don't announce some notifications. The behavior differs between the browser and is not reliably reproducible. Sadly, simple examples don't show the problem. Following site was of great help in understanding, what might be going on: https://tetralogical.com/blog/2024/05/01/why-are-my-live-regions-not-working/
My understanding is this: On `Notification.show("some text");` Vaadin generates this HTML in one go:
`<vaadin-notification-card aria-live="polite" role="alert" ...>some text</vaadin-notification-card>`

There are 2 problems, which interact with each other:

1. `role="alert"` shall only be used for critical event. On some platforms a screen reader announces such messages with the prefix Alert! or plays a specific earcon. That's a nice option, but shouldn't be the default in Vaadin.
2. The container with attribute aria-live has to appear in HTML first. Then later it's content has to be changed to the actual message. That's the only reliable way to trigger browser to fire the event screen readers are looking for. Granted, the ARIA spec isn't clear in this point. But apparently, this is how it is intended.

My educated guess: Vaadin adds always `role="alert"`, because this covers in part the problem of point 2. Without `role="alert"` notifications wouldn't be announced at all (with some exceptions like Firefox & JAWS).

Setting aria-live to "assertive" didn't help in our webapp. Probably because `role="alert"` is responsible for triggering the announcement right now.

### Expected outcome

- Screen readers shall always announce notifications, especially if `assertive=true`.
- `role="alert"` should be an option.

### Minimal reproducible example

I am unable to supply a simple example. But this workaround improved the reliability for notifications in our webapp:
```
        var noti = Notification.show("", DEFAULT_DURATION, DEFAULT_POSITION, true);
        UI ui = UI.getCurrent();
        ui.push();

        noti.setText(message);
```

### Steps to reproduce

Unknown.
In our webapp, Chrome has problems, when we change a lot of things in the view and at the same time create a notification. Firefox on the other hand doesn't announce a notification, when doing navigation to a different view at the same time (Notification has no parent, so it persists while changing the view).
Warning for tests: Having developer tools open in Firefox changed its behavior. I guess, that's s another hint, that this might be a timing related issue.

### Environment

Vaadin version(s): 24.7.6
OS: Windows 11 Version 23H2
NVDA 2024.4.2
Chrome Version 137.0.7151.104
Firefox 139.0.4 (64-Bit)

### Browsers

Chrome, Firefox

title: feat(voiceover): support VoiceOver Magic Tap (two-finger double-tap)
body:
Part of #3916 (seamless navigation whether or not a screen reader is enabled).

## Summary
The iOS VoiceOver **Magic Tap** — the two-finger double-tap that triggers an app's primary/context action (answer/end a call, play/pause media, start/stop recording, etc.) — is not supported. There is no `requestMagicTap` command on the iOS CtrlProxy client or in the runner protocol.

## Reference
- Parity design doc Gap 5: `docs/design-docs/mcp/a11y/voiceover-talkback-parity.md:84-92`.
- No `requestMagicTap` method exists on `IOSCtrlProxyClient` / `CtrlProxyVoiceOver`, and no magic-tap command string in `src/features/observe/ios/ctrlProxyRequestTypes.ts`.

## Why it matters
Magic Tap invokes `accessibilityPerformMagicTap()` on the app's responder chain — a distinct code path many apps implement for their primary action. Without it, AutoMobile can't drive or validate that behavior for VoiceOver users.

## Suggested direction
Add a `request_magic_tap` command in the Swift runner that dispatches `accessibilityPerformMagicTap()` (or synthesizes the two-finger double-tap), expose `requestMagicTap(...)` on the iOS client, and surface it via an MCP tool.

## Notes
iOS-specific; TalkBack has no Magic Tap equivalent, so this is not a parity-with-Android item.

_Captured during the iOS VoiceOver code/design-doc audit._

title: DatePicker is unusable with iOS VoiceOver
body:
### Description

When using the date picker with iOS VoiceOver:

1. It is not possible to navigate beyond the current month: the month list doesn't scroll, and the next calendar doesn't receive focus.
2. When navigating between date cells, VoiceOver announces only the day number (e.g. "10"), which makes it impossible to know where you are in the calendar

The cause is apparently the same for both: iOS VoiceOver uses its own grid/table navigation instead of moving the actual DOM focus, while the date picker relies on roving tabindex. As a result, the existing focus-based navigation logic is never triggered. In particular, calendars that don't contain the DOM focus are marked with `aria-hidden`, and since VoiceOver doesn't move the DOM focus, subsequent months remain `aria-hidden` and can't be reached with that type of navigation.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5898632a-2cb1-41b2-acf7-674a3866713c

title: [A11y] List: ripristino semantica liste su Safari/VoiceOver
body: ### Esiste già una discussione sul tema che ti interessa, o su un tema simile? - [x] Ho verificato e non esiste ### Versione della libreria main e 3.x ### Cosa L'attuale implementazione CSS di Bootstrap Italia causa la perdita della semantica di lista su sistemi Apple Safari + VoiceOver (macOS/iOS). A causa di un comportamento noto di WebKit (introdotto nel 2020), l'applicazione di list-style-type: none; rimuove la natura di "lista" per le tecnologie assistive. Di conseguenza, su Safari + VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), le liste non vengono annunciate come tali e gli item vengono letti in sequenza senza indicare il conteggio o la posizione. Segue il CSS attualmente presente in BSI che forza la rimozione dei bullet: ``` .it-list-wrapper .it-list { list-style-type: none; /* Rimuove la semantica su Safari */ margin: 0; padding: 0; } ``` ### Perché Garantire l'accessibilità su tutte le possibili combinazioni di browser e strumenti assistivi. Documentazione tecnica sul problema: [VoiceOver and Lists](https://www.scottohara.me/blog/2019/01/12/lists-and-safari.html) [Issue collegata su dev-kit-italia](https://github.com/italia/dev-kit-italia/issues/29) ### Contesto Safari e VoiceOver (macOS + iOS) ### Altro Per correggere questo problema in modo cross-browser e conforme ad ARIA senza dover aggiungere role duplicati, si potrebbe rimuovere il CSS indicato e invece agire sullo pseudo-element `::marker` per mantenere la semantica attiva pur nascondendo visivamente il punto elenco: ``` ul li::marker { font-size: 0px; } ``` https://caniuse.com/?search=%3A%3Amarker https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=204163 Test preliminari effettuati su Safari + VoiceOver confermano che questa modifica permette al lettore di schermo di annunciare correttamente: "You are currently on a list..." e il numero di elementi presenti. Sono da verificare i comportamenti di tutte le altre combinazioni browser/OS/screen reader

title: Provide keyboard access for layout block selection
body: The layout block selector uses a series of containers with radio inputs. As it is, the entire section is not keyboard accessible. We need to rework this into a group of buttons or accessible inputs to allow for keyboard navigation and selection.

title: Make each station card one accessibility element
body:
A station card's tap lives on the whole card, but every text and glyph inside it is its own accessibility element, so VoiceOver walks four to six stops per card and the platform audit reports each inner line as a small hit region (`AccessibilityAuditTests` exempts `chs-pending-*` and element-less reports for this reason).

One element per card fixes both: `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` on `activatable` in `StationListView.swift`, with a label that reads name, region, distance and status in that order.

The UI suite locates card text directly (`app.staticTexts["Friday Harbor"]`, the status strip by its full label), so those lookups move to the card element and a label match. Once it lands, drop the two exemptions in the audit test.

From #438.

title: Manual screen reader testing pass (VoiceOver + NVDA) after P1 a11y fixes
body:
## Why human

Static audit (`docs/design/ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT_2026-06.md`) covers code-verifiable criteria only; real AT behavior — ProseMirror announcement quality, live-region timing, focus perception — requires a human driving VoiceOver (macOS) and NVDA (Windows). Automated review typically surfaces a minority of real-world issues.

## Prerequisites

Issues #246, #247, #248, #249 merged.

## Test script (≈45 min per AT)

1. Open a `.md` with headings, lists, two tables, two Mermaid blocks, code blocks.
2. Tab into toolbar → arrow through buttons → activate Bold — verify name/role/state ("Bold, toggle button, pressed").
3. Navigate document content; verify heading levels and list semantics announce.
4. Enter a table grid: cell labels ("Row 2 column 3"), Enter-to-next-row focus announcement, add/delete row announcements via status line.
5. Mermaid block: verify diagram announces type label; toggle Mermaid setting off → gating message announces.
6. Trigger a command failure (add row with no table after deleting it) → verify assertive "Error:" interrupt.
7. Toggle source editor and back; verify no focus loss to body at any point.
8. Repeat key flows at 200% zoom and in a High Contrast theme.

## Deliverable

`docs/design/SR_TEST_RESULTS_<date>.md`: per-step pass/fail per AT, recordings where useful; file follow-up issues for failures (label `a11y`). On pass: update README with the conformance note (claim wording in MARKET_POSITION §3).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Results doc for both VoiceOver and NVDA committed
- [ ] Follow-up issues filed for every failure
- [ ] README conformance statement updated (or explicitly deferred with reason)

title: Windows: editor AutomationPeer — TextPattern + semantic span ranges for JAWS/NVDA (W7-1)
body:
Part of **Milestone W** — program: `docs/plans/18_windows_port/00_program.md`; spec: `docs/plans/18_windows_port/specs/w7_spec.md` (§W7-1). One PR per issue.

▶ Milestone W is **active** — W0–W6 delivered (W6-2 open for its human AT residual only); **W7 is the current wave** (banner refreshed 2026-09-16; spec revision `docs/plans/18_windows_port/specs/w7_spec.md` 2026-09-16 supersedes the 2026-08-09 note below where they differ).

Custom peer over the AvalonEdit host: TextPattern + semantic span descriptions (05 §6.4) from the same windowed span data the colorizer paints. Caret/selection events; line/word/char reading; span-boundary behavior verified on JAWS and NVDA separately. Lands with Wave 2. Depends on: W2-2 (#381).

---

## 2026-08-09 — Delivery spec (detailed; the W2-2 dependency is SATISFIED, the "lands with Wave 2" note is historical)

**Current state (verified).** W2-2 (#381) is CLOSED — the editor colorizer has consumed the canonical windowed span data since Wave 2, so the "one source, two consumers" precondition is real: this issue adds the second consumer. Wave 2 closed without this peer (the interleaving note is historical scheduling, not a live gate); it now lands standalone. Required reading, in-repo: `docs/plans/18_windows_port/specs/w_e7_rangefromchild_spike.md` (the RangeFromChild spike — the recorded UIA text-range groundwork) and 05 §6.4 (the semantic-span speech design). The reading surface's peer work (W3-1 and the #1088 fix) recorded a load-bearing lesson that applies here verbatim: **an AutomationPeer claimed by two parents dead-ends UIA navigation** — WPF stores one parent/index per peer, so structural peers must never re-hand children another peer already owns.

**Scope (deliverables).**

1. **The custom editor peer.** A peer for the AvalonEdit host exposing UIA `TextPattern`: document range, visible ranges, selection/caret ranges, `RangeFromPoint`/`RangeFromChild` (per the spike), text-unit movement (character/word/line) matching the buffer's actual line model.
2. **Semantic span exposure.** Span kind/role surfaced on text ranges (via attribute values and/or the 05 §6.4 description mechanism) from the SAME windowed span source the colorizer paints — wikilinks, tags, citations, embeds, code, math regions announce as VoiceOver does via the mac span consumer. No second span derivation (§W-G).
3. **Events.** Caret-moved and selection-changed UIA events raised correctly (screen-reader tracking depends on them); document-changed events on edits.
4. **Per-AT verification.** JAWS and NVDA behave differently around TextPattern — **both are acceptance targets, verified separately**: line/word/character reading, say-all, and span-boundary announcements. FlaUI-automatable assertions (TextPattern traversal, attribute reads, event ordering) go in the accessibility suite; what only a human pass can verify goes on the W7-4 checklist rows.

**Process.** Contracts doc BEFORE implementation (`docs/plans/34_editor_peer_contracts.md`): pin the text-unit semantics, the span-attribute mapping, event ordering, and the windowing behavior at range boundaries (what happens when a range extends past the materialized window — the spike's territory); then phased facts, red team per `docs/plans/24_red_team_protocol.md`, one PR, CI green, codoki.

**Acceptance / evidence.**
- FlaUI facts: TextPattern document/selection/visible ranges; RangeFromChild/RangeFromPoint per the spike; unit movement; span attributes at known offsets over a fixture note containing every span kind; caret/selection event assertions (cross-process, the W3-2 precedent shape).
- The #1088 double-parent regression cannot recur: a fact pinning navigation completeness across the peer's children (walk forward AND backward — the recorded diagnostic).
- `w_c_matrix.md` editor-row update (patterns column gains TextPattern + the span exposure); JAWS + NVDA human checklist rows recorded per W7-4.
- Known traps: CRLF format gate; the peers-with-two-parents rule; local

title: Add aria-label to facet show all/less toggle button for accessibility
body:
## Problem
The 'Show All' / 'Show Less' toggle button in facet cards lacks an aria-label attribute. This makes the button's purpose unclear to screen reader users, as they only hear the visible text without understanding the dynamic state change.

## Expected Behavior
The button should have a dynamic aria-label that clearly indicates the action:
- When collapsed: 'Show all facet options'
- When expanded: 'Show less facet options'

## Why This Matters
According to WCAG guidelines (particularly WCAG 2.1 Level A), all interactive elements should have clear, descriptive labels. This is especially important for buttons that toggle states, as screen reader users need to understand both what the button does and its current state.

## Affected Component
`src/routes/search/FacetCard.svelte` - the toggle button for showing all/less facet options

title: CBG/RBG helper and tooltip are not announced by Chrome/NVDA
body:
### What is the problem?

title: NVDA does not announce the `aria-required` attribute for the role `group`
body:
### What is the problem?

~~NVDA does not announce the `required` state for the checkbox-group in Firefox.~~

NVDA does not announce the `aria-required` attribute for components with the role `group` such as custom-field and checkbox-group. VoiceOver and JAWS, on the other hand, announce the attribute correctly, even for the `group` role.

The issue with NVDA apparently occurs because the `aria-required` attribute is not officially permitted for the `group` role according to [the ARIA docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/ARIA_Techniques/Using_the_aria-required_attribute#used_in_aria_roles).

title: [Bug] Issues with Select rendering and JAWS
body:
### 🐞 Describe the Bug

We've gotten reports that the JAWS is unable to correctly read minimal `select` element created with Ember. Specifically, when an option is selected, the selected value is _not_ read out by the screen reader. The workaround at the moment is to use aria-selected, but this seems problematic. Either JAWS has a bug, or Ember does, and we need to figure out which.

### 🔬 Minimal Reproduction

```hbs
{{!-- This example works --}}
<select>
  <option>Alabama</option>
  <option selected>California</option>
  <option>Oregon</option>
</select>

{{!-- This example does not work --}}
<select>
  {{#each values as |value|}}
    <option selected={{eq value this.selectedValue}}></option>
  {{/each}}
</select>
```

Codepen with the first example: https://codepen.io/pzuraq/pen/oNxGvWz

### 😕 Actual Behavior

The screen reader does not read out the option label.

### 🤔 Expected Behavior

The screen reader should read out the option label.

### 🌍 Environment

- Ember: Latest
- Node.js/npm: -
- OS: -
- Browser: -

### ➕ Additional Context

We've verified that the Ember version of the select is properly updating the _properties_ that represent the selected state, and other A11y tools including the A11y tree in Chrome work properly here. The next step is to start reducing the differences between these two examples to figure out what exactly is causing the issue.

Noted differences:

1. `selected` is set the first time as an _attribute_ on the native example. It remains set as the select is updated. By contrast, the Ember example always sets the _property_, so no option will have the attribute set at any time. We should see if removing the attribute in the native example causes any difference in behavior.
2. The Ember example will create its DOM dynamically, using `document.createElement` and manually appending it, whereas the native version does not. We should try to create a select using vanilla JS to see if that impacts behavior at all.

title: Test keyboard navigation for drag and drop interfaces
body:
This is a feature that addresses #1035, providing a keyboard navigation alternative to parts of the admin that use drag and drop patterns for manipulating trees. On the [`keyboard-drag-and-drop`](https://github.com/omeka/Omeka/tree/keyboard-drag-and-drop) branch, the current solution is implemented on the view for editing the site navigation (Appearance > Navigation). The functionality includes the following:
* Each navigation item should know have a keyboard button that opens a group of buttons for reordering. 
  * The user can move the navigation item up and down the tree. 
  * They can also nest the navigation item under a preceding node, or unnest from a parent node. 
  * After each reorder action, there should be a screen reader alert.
    * If the action fails, i.e. it can go no higher in the tree or cannot be nested further, there should be a general failure alert saying "Cannot reorder further."
    * If the action succeeds, it should announce 1) the navigation item reordered, and 2) the direction of reordering and most relevant node. For example: "Browse Items reordered. Moved above About."
* Activating the keyboard button should close the group of reorder actions and announce itself collapsed.

Test across desktop and mobile browsers with the usual suite of screen readers. Beyond feedback for testing functionality, this is also a good place for suggesting expanded features and improvements.

title: Accessibility enhancements: add role=application to body. Add explicit (hidden) link to launch full view
body:
Recent testing with a screen reader user has demonstrated two challenges I didn't anticipate in my earlier PR.
1. JAWS screen reader intercepts all keystrokes.  This can be alleviated by adding `role="application`" to the `<body>` element. This will enable JAWS users to traverse through the slides the same as other users. It also will have no negative impact on other users.
2. In order for screen reader users to present using Shower, they need to be able to launch the full slide view. Shower initially loads the slideshow in tiled format and users have to click on one of the slides in order to launch the full view. I think the easiest way to allow a screen reader user to launch the full view is to add a link (positioned offscreen) that allows the user to launch the first slide. 

@pepelsbey:  I'm interested in discussing how to handle these. Would you rather see these in HTML or would you want to see these parts added using JavaScript?  I see advantages to each approach. IMO adding this to Shower Core is more desirable so that we're 100% sure it is there for people who need it.

title: #General Accessibility issues
body:
I know that you guys invested a lot of efforts in the design and making of Runbox v7, but I'm sorry to say that the acessibility is vetry problematic.

The major problem comes from the `<canvas>` HTML element that you're using for the mails list. Canvases are made to display graphs and charts, i.e bitmap objects that do not carry information on their content. This means that acessibility tools (like JAWS) won't be able to access the canvas' content, and the emails can't be reached by using tab, space and other navigation keys.

The [Mozilla Developper Network page of the `<canvas>` element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Canvas_API/Tutorial/Hit_regions_and_accessibility) actually recommends against its use in acessible websites and apps:
> The <canvas> element on its own is just a bitmap and does not provide information about any drawn objects. Canvas content is not exposed to accessibility tools like semantic HTML is. In general, you should avoid using canvas in an accessible website or app.

Another issue of canvases is that they don't respect the color scheme of the browser (in the case of a high contrast theme, as shown below), nor the other browser styles, like the font size:
[image]

---

There is a problem too with the folders list on the left, and the "compose", "draft" and "v7 buttons. They cannot be accedd via navigation keys either


**So can you please take this into account in Runbox v7? Thanks!**

title: Add accessibility labels to all interactive elements
body:
## Summary

None of the \`TouchableOpacity\` and \`Pressable\` elements in OMNYX have \`accessibilityLabel\` or \`accessibilityRole\` props. Screen readers like TalkBack (Android) are completely broken. This issue tracks adding proper labels across all tab screens.

## What to add

Every interactive element needs at minimum:

\`\`\`tsx
<TouchableOpacity
  accessibilityRole="button"
  accessibilityLabel="Start device scan"
  accessibilityHint="Scans all installed apps for permission risks"
>
\`\`\`

## Screens to cover

This issue can be split into separate PRs, one per screen:

- [ ] \`app/(tabs)/intelligence.tsx\` -- scan button, rescan, quick actions
- [ ] \`app/(tabs)/threat-feed.tsx\` -- filter buttons, mark resolved, request analysis
- [ ] \`app/(tabs)/agents.tsx\` -- no interactive elements currently, verify
- [ ] \`app/(tabs)/replay.tsx\` -- verify no interactive elements missing labels
- [ ] \`app/(tabs)/modes.tsx\` -- mode selection buttons
- [ ] \`app/(tabs)/settings.tsx\` -- all settings controls
- [ ] \`app/(tabs)/index.tsx\` -- home screen buttons

## Acceptance criteria

- All buttons have \`accessibilityRole="button"\`
- All buttons have a descriptive \`accessibilityLabel\`
- Complex actions include an \`accessibilityHint\`

title: Alle Komponenten: aria-describedby, aria-labelledby und aria-details müssen von außen nutzbar sein (Shadow DOM)
body:
Alle KoliBri-Komponenten sollen die Attribute `aria-describedby`, `aria-labelledby` und `aria-details` anbieten, damit äußere (hostende) Komponenten per Standard-ARIA-Mechanismus Verknüpfungen zu KoliBri-Komponenten herstellen können. **Aktuell ist das nicht möglich, weil die ARIA-Attribute bzw. IDs aus der Shadow DOM-Struktur der KoliBri-Komponente nicht heraus nach außen referenziert werden können.**

**Erwartetes Ziel:**
- Jede KoliBri-Komponente besitzt die Möglichkeit, dass ARIA-Attribute von außen (z.B. durch Host-Komponenten) gesetzt und von Assistenz-Technologien gelesen werden können.
- Die Durchleitung der Attribute durch den Shadow DOM wird zuverlässig gewährleistet. 
- Dokumentation und Beispiele zeigen, wie übergreifende Barrierefreiheit über Komponenten-Grenzen hinaus umzusetzen ist.

**Kontext & Verknüpfte Issues:**
- #9073 - aria-describedby wird bei Inputs mit _msg und _hasCounter nicht korrekt gesetzt
- #8657 - Feature: aria-details für die InputFelder
- #8608 - Unterschiedliche Tooltip- und aria-label-Texte für bessere Barrierefreiheit ermöglichen

Bitte um Umsetzung aller KoliBri-Komponenten.

*Dieses Issue ist ein Meta-Issue für barrierefreie, component-übergreifende ARIA-Verknüpfungen.*

title: accessibility: use talkback actions as alternative to the bottom sheet on long-press
body:
### Your use case

#### What would you like to do?

I would like to have an easier way to access message actions, such as react, reply, etc

#### Why would you like to do it?

Screenreader users, especially on mobile, are inconvenienced a lot by UI clutter. For example, having to swipe right three or so times to get to the next message in the timeline is a problem, so is having to long double press, then wait for the timeout to pass, only then finally being focused on the bottom sheet with options

#### How would you like to achieve it?

For this, [accessibility actions](https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/androidx/core/view/accessibility/AccessibilityNodeInfoCompat.AccessibilityActionCompat) are the best fit for what I'm describing.

The screenreader knows how to use them, and more specifically, it emulates better what users have had on ios for a long time for decluttering UI, namely the rotor, where elements are a single swipe targets and, instead of each option being swipe targets after that element, they are incapsulated in those actions one could reach by spinning the rotor to actions and then flicking up and down to select the required action, then double-tapping to confirm.

For more information, see [this part of an article from android developer documentation](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/ui/accessibility/principles#accessibility-actions)

### Have you considered any alternatives?

well, the only alternative is using swipe targets like we did up to this point, with the bottom sheet activating on long press. While better than the every option is a swipe target method, it still requires waiting around for the timeout to pass, which could be frustrating if you have to do an action to afew messages, not just one per minute or so

### Additional context

_No response_

### Are you willing to provide a PR?

No

title: Divider: render decorative by default instead of always exposing a separator
body:
Source: `docs/audits/divider.md` **DV1**.

Every `Divider` renders `<hr role="separator" aria-orientation="…">`, so each one is announced as a separator (real-browser aria snapshot of the InList story: `text, separator, text, separator, text`; also the SideSheet `showDivider` header line).

- m3 divider/accessibility: "Dividers are **decorative elements**, which have no contrast minimums."
- Compose `HorizontalDivider` / `VerticalDivider`: a bare `Canvas` + `drawLine`, **no semantics** (invisible to TalkBack).
- `role="separator"` on `<hr>` is redundant (implicit role), and `aria-orientation="horizontal"` is the default.

Proposed (API decision): make decorative the default (`aria-hidden` / `role="none"`), with an opt-in for a semantic thematic break (e.g. a `decorative={false}` prop or passing `role="separator"`), keeping `aria-orientation="vertical"` only for the semantic vertical case. Do not touch `MenuDivider` (separator inside `role="menu"` is correct there).

**VRT impact**: none (accessibility tree only).

title: fix(textfield): expose prefix/suffix and character counter to assistive tech
body:
From `docs/audits/textfield.md` **T2 / T3** (bundled — both change the input's `aria-describedby` wiring).

**T2 — prefix/suffix not associated with the input.** They are bare `<span>`s; a screen reader focusing the input never hears e.g. "$" or "kg". m3.material.io accessibility: "The accessibility label for prefix and suffix needs to have a unique id attribute". Compose attaches text semantics so TalkBack reads prefix, text and suffix together. → give prefix/suffix ids and reference them from the input's `aria-describedby`.

**T3 — counter has no accessible label.** The counter `3 / 20` is read verbatim via `aria-describedby`. m3.material.io accessibility: the remaining-character counter "should be called 'character count' within the label". → add visually hidden wording (e.g. "character count 3 of 20") while keeping the visible `3 / 20`.

Tests: assert the accessible description includes the prefix/suffix and the counter wording (`toHaveAccessibleDescription`).

**VRT impact:** none (visually hidden text only).

title: [Feature Request] Add aria-disabled attribute to disabled VBtn components for improved accessibility
body: ### Problem to solve Currently, when a v-btn component is disabled using the disabled prop, it only applies visual styling (CSS classes) and prevents interactions, but lacks proper ARIA attributes for accessibility. This creates several issues: Screen readers cannot properly announce the disabled state to users with visual impairments Automated testing becomes difficult when trying to target disabled buttons Does not follow WCAG 2.1 accessibility guidelines for disabled interactive elements Inconsistent with modern web accessibility standards that recommend using aria-disabled="true" instead of or alongside the disabled attribute ``` ``` ``` ``` This issue is part of a broader accessibility improvement effort. Similar issues may exist in other components like: v-text-field (disabled inputs) v-select (disabled selectors) v-checkbox (disabled checkboxes) Time picker clock items (already reported separately) Visual error in storybook testing ### Proposed solution Add the aria-disabled="true" attribute to VBtn components when the disabled prop is set to true. This should be implemented in the VBtn component to: Automatically add aria-disabled="true" when disabled prop is true Ensure the attribute is not present when the button is enabled Maintain backward compatibility with existing implementations Follow the same pattern used in other Vuetify components that support disabled states

title: [E37-K01] Spike: validate the graph library for 200-node fps and keyboard connect
body:
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Key | E37-K01 |
| Kind | Spike |
| Estimate | 2 |
| Sprint | Sprint 14 |
| Component | web |
| Phase | P3 Drawing & Alerts |
| Priority | P0 Critical |
| Perspective | Architecture |
| Risk | R8 Browser/GPU compat |
| Parent | E37 |
| Blocked by | E35-K01, E35-T01, E35-T02, E35-T03, E35-T04 |

## Context
`docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-146 names React Flow / Rete.js as the preferred candidates *specifically because they render nodes as real DOM elements*, which is what makes the mandated DOM-mirror a11y strategy possible. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2 names React Flow for E37. But the two binding non-functional requirements have never been measured against the chosen library: **200 nodes at 60 fps** (SCR-082 §Performance) and a **fully keyboard-operable connect flow** (US-RULE-005, CMP-237). If React Flow cannot meet both without heroic customisation, the whole of E37-S01/S02/S05 is mis-scoped, and we need to know before Sprint 17 starts.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §5 applies: this spike answers questions and produces an ADR, not shippable code.

## Scope / Deliverables
Timebox: **4 working days**, agreed with the Architect.

Questions to answer:
1. Does React Flow (current major version, pinned) sustain **60 fps pan/zoom on a 200-node / ~260-edge graph** on the reference hardware in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1, inside Electron and Chromium, with our node chrome (not stock demo nodes)?
2. Can nodes, ports and edges each be made individually focusable with roving tabindex, without fighting the library's own pointer-first interaction layer, and can a **keyboard connect** (focus output port → `Enter` → arrow to target port → `Enter`) be implemented on top of the library's controlled state?
3. Does the library's controlled `nodes`/`edges` model let `packages/rule-graph` own state fully, so `graph_layout` can be persisted separately from the IR and excluded from the canonical hash?
4. What does auto-layout cost? Measure a layout library (`elkjs` vs `dagre`) on 60- and 200-node graphs: wall-clock, main-thread block time, and whether it must run in a worker.
5. Bundle cost of the editor route (library + layout + our code), gzipped, to confirm it can be lazily code-split out of the initial bundle (budget #9).
6. Fallback assessment of Rete.js on the same criteria, sufficient to make a decision rather than a guess.

Decision criteria agreed up front:
- If (1) fails below **45 fps** at 200 nodes after one round of reasonable optimisation (virtualised node rendering, memoised edges), the scope of SCR-082 is reduced to a documented node cap (e.g. 120 nodes with a warning beyond it) rather than switching library late — and that cap is written into SCR-082 and E37-S01.
- If (2) requires forking the library, React Flow is rejected in favour of Rete.js or a thin in-house node layer, and E37-S01/S02 are re-estimated before Sprint 17 planning.
- If (4) blocks the main thread >100 ms at 200 nodes, auto-layout moves to a web worker in E37-T02 by default.

Deliverables: a throwaway prototype branch, a benchmark table (fps p50/p95, layout time, block time, bundle delta), a keyboard-connect proof-of-concept recording, and an ADR.

## Out of scope
- Production-quality components, styling against the design tokens, or any IR integration beyond a hard-coded sample graph.
- Evaluating graph libraries not shortlisted in the component catalogue.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All six questions answered with recorded evidence
  When the timebox ends
  Then each question has a written answer backed by a benchmark number, a code snippet or a recording, and no question is left as an opinion

Scenario: The fps question is answered on a realistic graph
  Given a 200-node graph using our real node chrome and edge styling
  When pan and zoom are exercised for 60 seconds
  Then p50 and p95 frame times are recorded in Electron and C

It's difficult to drag them only minute amounts from where they are, and pretty much impossible to a particular number. For example:I know I want to practice a solo at 60% speed. I suggest that chording a key with the up and down arrows adjust the sliders by 5% up or down. For example, nothing for speed, V for volume, D for difficulty, etc. If that't not friendly-enough to i18n, then using SHIFT and CTRL could work as well.

title: Keyboard a11y issues (etc.) across nav layouts
body: https://github.com/omeka-s-themes/foundation/issues/78 discusses issues with the menu pattern for accordion menus on this theme (applicable to both the off-canvas menu on smaller viewports and the vertical menu layout available via the full height column nav configuration). This issue focuses on larger keyboard accessibility issues (and a few other bugs) across Foundation's menus on both the horizontal dropdown and full height column patterns. For the horizontal dropdown: - Screen reader function looks good here, although with keyboard alone, it is impossible to actually activate any menu item with a dropdown toggle (parent or child). However, they can be interacted with, opening dropdowns down through the nav structure (until reaching an item without a toggle that can be activated appropriately), so I think this is fundamentally an issue with the toggles and menu items being one and the same. - For both screen reader and keyboard nav, dropdowns do not close automatically after tabbing away from them (unless a separate dropdown parent item is activated). For the full height column: - Some toggles are not visible, though they do function appropriately: This is true for all stylesheets. - After opening and then closing the off-canvas menu, the search bar disappears from the full height column nav. - Search bar placeholder text is not always in full view (e.g. on Chrome, on viewports zoomed 100%+): True to both: - On desktop, when the off-canvas menu is activated from a small enough viewport and the viewport is then widened without first closing the menu, the off-canvas menu remains open (so two types of nav menus appear on screen), and the screen gains horizontal scroll: - Same issue as the theme on Classic, https://github.com/omeka/theme-foundation/issues/69: Focus can move outside of the off-canvas menu to elements on the page, not all of which are in view (and all of which are dimmed). I'm thinking it makes more sense to make all exterior content hidden while adding a close menu toggle directly into the off-canvas menu.

title: [Feature] Skip-to-content link and a focus target on `<main>`

There is no skip link anywhere in the app, and `<main>` has no `id` or `tabIndex` to jump to.

**Files**

- `apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx:29-38`
- `apps/web/src/components/layout/navbar.tsx:66-102`
- `apps/web/src/components/app/app-tabs.tsx`
