title: Keep focus inside a popover when it positions again while open
body:
## Context

While investigating alternative designs for #7614, which fixes #7612, a prototype that changed how `Popover` releases its initial focus showed that a popup takes its initial focus again after every positioning pass that runs while it is open. A separate check confirmed the behavior on `main` in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.

## Problem

`Popover` marks each positioning pass as unplaced ([`popover.tsx#L331-L340`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/blob/42ce68deb671a7330a0e83b215daec4c02174f2b/packages/ariakit-react-components/src/popover/popover.tsx#L331-L340)) and passes `autoFocusOnShow: positioned && autoFocusOnShow` to `Dialog` ([`popover.tsx#L642`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/blob/42ce68deb671a7330a0e83b215daec4c02174f2b/packages/ariakit-react-components/src/popover/popover.tsx#L642)). When a pass ends, the value turns back on, so the `Dialog` auto-focus effect ([`dialog.tsx#L506-L588`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/blob/42ce68deb671a7330a0e83b215daec4c02174f2b/packages/ariakit-react-components/src/dialog/dialog.tsx#L506-L588)) runs again and focuses the popup's initial target. The effect keeps focus only when it has left the popup, so focus that the user moved inside the popup goes back to the initial target.

A pass runs again when a dependency of the positioning effect changes ([`popover.tsx#L510-L536`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/blob/42ce68deb671a7330a0e83b215daec4c02174f2b/packages/ariakit-react-components/src/popover/popover.tsx#L510-L536)). Examples are `store.render()`, the anchor element, `placement`, an arrow element that mounts, and props such as `gutter` or `sameWidth`. A viewport resize, a page scroll, or content growth goes through Floating UI's `autoUpdate` and does not run the effect again, so focus stays.

## Reproduction

```tsx
import * as Ariakit from "@ariakit/react";

export default function Example() {
  const menu = Ariakit.useMenuStore();
  return (
    <>
      <Ariakit.MenuButton store={menu}>Actions</Ariakit.MenuButton>
      <Ariakit.Menu store={menu}>
        <Ariakit.MenuItem>Item one</Ariakit.MenuItem>
        <Ariakit.MenuItem>Item two</Ariakit.MenuItem>
        <Ariakit.MenuItem>Item three</Ariakit.MenuItem>
      </Ariakit.Menu>
    </>
  );
}
```

1. Focus the Actions button and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. Item one has focus.
2. Press <kbd>ArrowDown</kbd> twice. Item three has focus.
3. While focus stays in the menu, call `menu.render()` from outside the menu, or change its `placement` or `gutter`.

Observed: focus goes back to Item one. Expected: focus stays on Item three.

The `menu-placing-pass` sandbox shows the same result with its Reposition button. Other popups behave the same way:

- A menu opened with a click sends focus back to the menu container and clears the active item.
- A `Popover` moves focus from its second button back to its first one.
- A `Hovercard` opened through `HovercardDisclosure` moves focus from its second link back to its first one.
- A `ComboboxSelect` makes the selected item active again. #7614 covers this case for a keyboard move.

## Pre-existing on main

Yes. It reproduces on `main` at [`42ce68d`](https://github.com/ariakit/ariakit/commit/42ce68deb671a7330a0e83b215daec4c02174f2b) in Chrome, Firefox, and Safari with `Menu`, `Popover`, `Hovercard`, and `ComboboxSelect`. The reproductions used temporary sandboxes only.

## Why #7614 can finish without it

#7614 keeps a keyboard move in a `ComboboxSelect` popup, including one made before a later positioning pass, by passing the moved item as the initial focus. The repeated initial focus comes from `Popover` and affects every popover, so a fix for it is independent.

## Expected outcome

A popup takes its initial focus once each time it opens. A later positioning pass does not move focus that is already inside the popup.

## Notes for the fix

- The `menu-placing-pass` tests already describe this model: "an already open popup has no initial focus left to take" ([`test-browser.ts#L21

## Summary
On `apps/web/app/dashboard/page.tsx` and `apps/web/app/marketplace/page.tsx`, choosing a row in `InvoiceTable` sets `selectedInvoice`, and the resulting `InvoiceCard` / action panel renders in a `lg:col-span-4` sidebar. Below the `lg` breakpoint that grid collapses to one column, so the sidebar is placed after the table (and on the dashboard after the whole "On-Chain Activity Logs" block). On a phone the user taps a row, sees only a highlight, and has to discover the panel by scrolling past the table and activity log. Nothing moves focus, scrolls the panel into view or announces that the console changed; screen-reader users get no cue at all. The dashboard's `AnimatePresence` swap also changes the content under a fixed heading ("Management console").

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Below `lg`, selecting an invoice scrolls the console into view (respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`) and moves focus to its heading (`tabIndex={-1}`)
- [ ] Alternatively present the console as a bottom sheet/dialog on small screens with a clear close control and proper `role="dialog"` semantics
- [ ] A polite live region announces "Invoice INV#... selected, actions available below"
- [ ] Verify at 375px on both routes and add a Playwright check

## Tech Stack
Next.js, `apps/web/app/dashboard/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/marketplace/page.tsx`

## Notes
Bottom-sheet versus scroll-into-view is a UX decision; either satisfies the acceptance criteria.

title: Modal not trapping focus
body:
Package version (if known): any
Semantic UI modal, does not work properly i.e. when the modal is opened, the focus remains in the background instead of being trapped inside of the modal. We are wondering if you are aware of this issue and if you have considered how this could be resolved, because it is a fairly big usability issue. 

## Describe the bug
In some modals in invenio code, you are kind of bypassing this issue, by using autoFocus on some element inside of the modal and then when the modal opens, the tabulation does start from this point, however, if you keep tabbing you again end up in the background - so this is not a really sustainable solution.

If I remember correctly, you guys are taking some notes of problematic elements in SUI and you will be looking for some way how to fix it (I think dropdown is another problematic element). The goal of this issue is primarily to see if you are aware of this and if there are some plans/ideas how to tackle this issue. Please let us know and thanks!

## Steps to Reproduce
You can reproduce it in any modal, though as mentioned, you usually put autofocus on some element, so you would have a situation when tabbing does start in the modal, but then it runs out of the modal into  the background.
## Expected behavior
When modal opens, tabbing (focus) would start inside and stay trapped inside the modal while it is open.

title: FabMenu: focus order, menu keyboard pattern and focus restore
body:
Source: `docs/audits/fab-menu.md` **FM2** + **FM3** (same keyboard/focus code in `FabMenu.tsx`).

**FM2 — focus order / keys.** The list precedes the toggle in DOM order, so while open Tab from the toggle leaves the component and Shift+Tab reaches the items bottom-up (measured). The list is `role="menu"` but has no Arrow/Home/End handling or roving tabindex.
Expected: m3.material.io a11y — "initial focus remains on the close button … Then the focus moves from the top menu item to the bottom" (close button → 1st → 2nd → 3rd), and on web "follow the accessibility guidelines for FABs and menus". Compose moves focus from the toggle into the items on Tab / Down (FloatingActionButtonMenu.kt:137-153), and the sample returns to the toggle on Up / Shift+Tab. So: toggle first in DOM order (visual position unchanged), ArrowDown/Tab from the open toggle → top item, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End within the items (APG menu), Up/Shift+Tab from the first item → toggle.

**FM3 — focus restore.** Escape (and activating an item) closes the menu but leaves focus on the now-hidden item (measured). Expected: focus returns to the toggle (APG menu button; Compose sample closes back to the button).

**VRT impact:** none.

title: fix(a11y): graph canvases offer no keyboard path to focus or activate a node
body:
Extracted from `BACKLOG.md` (**#124**, opened 2026-07-18, source "UX flows review") during the autonomous backlog sweep on 2026-08-07. The backlog ID stays retired per `agent_docs/backlog_process.md` rule 8 (never reuse an ID).

## Finding (original entry)

> Graph canvases are mouse/touch-only: no tabIndex/role/aria fallback, no keyboard path to focus a node or open its popup. Large item — needs a design (roving virtual focus or DOM shadow list).

## Current state (re-verified 2026-08-07)

The `role`/`aria` half of the original finding has since been addressed — both canvases now carry a static description:

- `src/components/GraphViewer.tsx` — `role="img"` + `aria-label="Tag graph: N tags, M connections"`
- `src/components/StashGraphCanvas.tsx` — `role="img"` + `aria-label="Stash graph: N nodes, M edges"`

What remains open is the interaction half, and it is the larger part:

- Neither `<canvas>` is focusable (no `tabIndex`), so the keyboard cannot reach the graph at all.
- There is no way to move a selection between nodes, and no key that opens the node popup a click produces.
- Everything reachable only from that popup is therefore keyboard-unreachable: analyse / end analysis, ignore / re-include a tag, track / stop tracking a tag, jump to a stash.
- The surrounding controls (zoom buttons, tag search, focus/highlight clearing, legend) are already keyboard-operable — the gap is the canvas itself.

## Why this needs a design, not a patch

A canvas has no DOM children, so assistive technology has nothing to walk. The two established options both cut across the render loop:

1. **Roving virtual focus** — hold one `activeNodeId` in state, make the canvas `tabIndex={0}`, move the selection with the arrow keys, and mirror the active node into `aria-activedescendant` plus a visually-hidden live region that announces it. Needs a deterministic node ordering: the layout is force-directed, so screen position drifts every frame and "the node to the right" is not stable.
2. **DOM shadow list** — render a visually-hidden `<ul>` of focusable node entries next to the canvas and drive the existing popup from it. Cheaper to get correct, but it duplicates the node set and has to stay in sync with the filtering / analysis state.

Either way the popup then needs a focus trap (`src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts` already exists and is used by SearchOverlay / KeyboardShortcutsHelp / MermaidDiagram) and focus restoration back to the canvas on close.

## Scope

Too large for a backlog sweep: the two components are already 1820 and 1944 LoC, and the change touches component state, the rAF draw loop and the popup surface at once. Filing it so it can be scheduled and designed deliberately.

Related: #457 (roving tabindex for tab bars) — same roving-focus pattern on a different surface.

body: As a **user**, I want to be able to **focus** on stepper elements, so that I can clearly **see which step I’m currently on and navigate** between steps. ### Acceptance Criteria **1. Focus Visibility** - Given I am navigating with a keyboard - When I tab to a stepper item that has been complete or is the current step item - Then a visible focus indicator must appear on that step. **2. Meets Accessibility Contrast Requirements** - Given a focus indicator is displayed - Then the focus outline must have at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours (WCAG 2.2 Focus Visible). - Use colour #0535D2 as it is used as the focus indicator for GC Design **3. Current Step is Programmatically Identified** - Given I have focused on a stepper item - When that item is the active or current step - Then it must be programmatically indicated using aria-current="step" or an equivalent pattern. **4. Navigating a Step** - Given a stepper item is focused - When I press Enter or Space - Then that step becomes active and the page for that step is displayed. **5. Skipped or Disabled Steps** - Given a step is disabled or skipped (see related ticket INSERT HERE) - Then it must not receive focus. - And the focus order must not break (focus moves to the next available step). **6. Screen Reader Expectations** - Given I use a screen reader - When I navigate the stepper - Then each step must announce: - Step number - Step name - Whether it is current, completed, or skipped

title: [harness-feedback] contrast.py cannot resolve token chains into imported scales, so COL-2-compliant repos get mostly-manual A11Y-1
body:
## The ask

`checks/contrast.py` resolves token values only from the single file named in `DESIGN.md`'s `Tokens` → `source:` bullet. When a semantic token is a `var()` indirection onto a scale **imported** into that file, the chain dead-ends and the pair falls out of automated grading. Please resolve `var()` chains through the stylesheets that `source:` `@import`s — including into `node_modules` — or let a repo declare extra resolution paths.

## What surfaced it

`dx-design-language` run on `String-sg/design-teacher-workspace` (Teacher Workspace), 2026-09-01, adding a `pairs:` declaration to the `Colour` section for the first time. An earlier design ticket in that repo had recorded `contrast.py` as entirely inert there for want of `pairs:`, so every A11Y-1 verdict was manual. Declaring `pairs:` activated the check — and then 4 of 5 pairs still went to manual.

## Evidence

```
$ python3 checks/contrast.py .
NOTE  contrast: path arguments are not scanned — this check grades the token pairs declared in DESIGN.md
ERROR contrast: declared pair [--foreground, --background] could not resolve --foreground, --background in src/styles.css — that pair goes to manual verification
ERROR contrast: declared pair [--muted-foreground, --background] could not resolve --muted-foreground, --background in src/styles.css — that pair goes to manual verification
ERROR contrast: declared pair [--muted-foreground, --card] could not resolve --muted-foreground, --card in src/styles.css — that pair goes to manual verification
ERROR contrast: declared pair [--ring, --background] could not resolve --background in src/styles.css — that pair goes to manual verification
EXIT: 0
```

Cause, in `src/styles.css`:

```css
@import '@radix-ui/colors/slate.css';   /* --slate-1..12 live in node_modules */
:root {
  --background: var(--slate-1);
  --foreground: var(--slate-12);
  --card: white;
}
```

`--slate-12` is never defined in `src/styles.css`, so the chain cannot close. The one pair that *does* resolve is `[--primary-foreground, --primary]`, because both ends are literal in that file (`--primary: var(--twblue-9)`, `--twblue-9: #0064ff`) — measured 4.92:1 against white, passes AA.

## Why it matters

A11Y-1 is **L0**, and the pattern that defeats the resolver is the one COL-2 mandates: *"Functional colours (success/warning/danger) come from the shared Radix Colors scales."* A consumer repo that follows COL-2 imports those scales rather than redefining them, so the check is weakest exactly where the catalogue is most prescriptive. Teacher Workspace imports six Radix scales this way.

Note this is a **precision** gap, not a correctness bug: the check fails honestly, naming each unresolved pair and routing it to manual verification rather than reporting a false pass.

## Suggested fix

1. Follow `@import` statements from `tokens.source` and parse the imported files too, resolving module specifiers (`@radix-ui/colors/slate.css`) against `node_modules`.
2. Or add an optional `resolve-paths:` bullet to the `Tokens` section for repos whose scales live elsewhere.

Option 1 needs no `DESIGN.md` change in any consumer repo and would close the chain for every product on the Radix pattern.

title: ProblemHeader: Subheader Color Contrast
body:
The subHeader (`class=“subHeader”`) contains a mahogany (#db6f00) colored background. The text within the subHeader is white (#ffffff), creating a contrast ratio of 3.34:1. 

While the content is fairly large, it does not quite meet the minimum size for “large” text (14pt and bold), as it is 14px and not bold. While the text could be enlarged to meet these minimums, the serifs on the numbers and the small scale of some of the mathematical operators (notably the - ) are sometimes difficult to make out. 
#### Suggested Solution
Darkening the background will ensure that all users will have a more readable experience for this content. A slightly darker hue for the subHeader, such as #b05e00, will provide a sufficient color contrast ratio (in this case, 4.72:1).

title: Toastify: Notification Color Contrast
body:
The toastify components are used to present users with notifications. The colors for various states have been updated from the toastify defaults, but these new colors (with the exception of the error content) are below the 4.5:1 required for normal sized text.

The text for all toastify notifications are presented in white (#ffffff). The background color for warnings (`class=“Toastify__toast--warning”`) is an orange (#f89406) which has a color contrast ratio of 2.28:1. Success messages (`class=“Toastify__toast--success”`) have a light green (#51a351) background which has a color contrast ratio of 3.13:1. Finally, generic info notes (`class=“Toastify__toast--info”`) have a teal (#2f96b4) background which has a color contrast ratio of 3.42:1.

#### Suggested Solution
Each of the listed background colors would have a sufficient color contrast ratio (in every case at least 6.0:1) if their text color were changed to black (#000000). However, if keeping the white text is preferred, each background color could be darkened until a sufficient color contrast ratio is attained.

title: StateArt announces fixed English alt text that is wrong wherever an illustration is reused
body:
## Problem

`StateArt` gives each illustration one fixed English alt sentence, and none of its 13 call sites overrides it. The art is reused in places where that sentence is wrong:

- The `empty-leaderboard` art also appears in the quiet dashboard stat strip, the People "No one goes by @x" and "Discover the network" states, and `/score`'s no-reputation page. All of them are announced as "No one on the leaderboard yet — be the first".
- The `vouch-sent` art illustrates the empty activity feed and the empty pending-cards panel. Both are announced as "Vouch sent — their star is waiting to be claimed", the opposite of the state.

Turkish users always hear English. In most of these spots the visible heading already describes the state, and some uses are small ornaments (e.g. the 64px streak fire). `Sticker` already defaults to `alt=""` with `aria-hidden`; `StateArt` doesn't.

**Files**

- `apps/web/src/components/ui/state-art.tsx:5-13`
- `apps/web/src/components/ui/state-art.tsx:36`

title: Implement an automated function at a core level to append alt-text to images that do not already have them
body:
An accessibility gain which could be mandated by the core software without requiring additional effort from community system and module developers. Screen readers rely upon the use of the `alt=""` property to report what an image is. All images in FVTT presently have a title attribute which traditionally matches the name of the element with which it is associated by way of the "title" attribute. By using the same logic used to apply the title attributes, we can provide alt text accessibility by making `alt="An image depicting ${title}"`

This would bring screen reader compatibility for thousands of images included in systems as well as the core software.

title: a11y: run the a11y config across all pages and fix top violations
body:
## Background

The repo has a dedicated accessibility gate (`eslint.config.a11y.mjs`, applying `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` recommended rules via `npm run a11y`), but the current violations across pages aren't tracked or driven down.

## Why this matters

Accessibility is both an ethical baseline and (for an education platform) often a requirement. A one-time audit + fix of the top violations makes the a11y gate meaningful (see #490 to make it blocking).

## Suggested approach

1. Run `npm run a11y` across `components` and `app` and collect the violations.
2. Group by rule (labels, roles, alt text, focus order, etc.).
3. Fix the top/most-common violations; file any large ones as follow-ups.
4. Coordinate with #490 (make the gate fail CI) so it stays clean afterward.

## Files to touch

- Wherever violations are found (broad).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run a11y` violations are enumerated and the top ones fixed.
- [ ] Remaining large items are filed as follow-ups.

## How to test

- `npm run a11y` (violation count drops to the agreed baseline).

## Out of scope

- The specific `img`/caption/deps items (#548–#550).

## References

- `eslint.config.a11y.mjs`; #490 (make gate blocking).

I'm trying to figure out the best way to meet our accessibility standards for time-based media and it's a bit tricky with the available options, and I think tricky to even conceptualize in some ways. title: Missing alternative text field for images
body:
### What’s broken?

When inserting an image in the Docs editor, no field allows providing alternative text. Only a caption is offered, which does not substitute for alternative text.

### What did you expect to happen?

A dedicated alternative text field, distinct from the caption, must be available in the image editing panel. Its value must be reflected in the alt attribute of the generated  element.

### Steps to reproduce

Open a Docs document
Insert an image via / or the toolbar
Open the image editing panel
Notice that no alternative text field is available, only a caption field
Possible solution

Add an "Alternative text" field in the image editing panel, distinct from the caption field.
Additional context / Screenshots

The caption is visible content associated with the image; it does not replace alternative text, which is transmitted to assistive technologies and must describe the content or function of the image.

WCAG Criteria

[Criterion 1.1: Does each informative image have alternative text?](https://accessibilite.numerique.gouv.fr/methode/criteres-et-tests/#1.1)

Impact

A blind user navigating with a screen reader inserts an image and has no way to provide alternative text. The image will be rendered without accessible description for users relying on assistive technologies.

title: Add aria-label to wallet connect button in Navbar
body:
## Difficulty: Easy

## Summary
The wallet connect/disconnect button rendered inside `components/Navbar.tsx` and `components/WalletButton.tsx` is missing a descriptive `aria-label` attribute, making it ambiguous for screen-reader users.

## Task
Add a meaningful `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) to the wallet connect/disconnect button so assistive technologies can announce it clearly.

## Detailed Description
In `components/WalletButton.tsx`, the primary `<button>` element that triggers the wallet provider modal currently relies solely on its visible text content. When the button is in a `connecting` or icon-only state (e.g., on mobile where only a truncated address is shown), the accessible name is either empty or confusing. The i18n translation keys `wallet.connect`, `wallet.connecting`, and `wallet.disconnect` already exist in `messages/en.json`, `messages/fr.json`, and `messages/sw.json` — they just need to be wired to the `aria-label` attribute so the accessible name tracks the button's current state.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The wallet button always has a non-empty `aria-label` that accurately reflects its current state (connect / connecting / disconnect).
- [ ] The `aria-label` value is sourced from the existing i18n translation keys (`wallet.connect`, `wallet.connecting`, `wallet.disconnect`) to support all three locales (en, fr, sw).
- [ ] Running `npm run test` passes; the existing `WalletButton` snapshot test (if any) is updated if the DOM changes.
- [ ] No console accessibility warnings are introduced.

## Notes
- File to modify: `components/WalletButton.tsx`
- Related translation keys are already in `messages/en.json` — no new translation strings needed.
- The `useTranslations` hook from `next-intl` is already used elsewhere in the component tree.

title: a11y(web): NotificationBell does not expose its unread count or popup semantics to assistive tech
body:
## Summary
`apps/web/components/shared/NotificationBell.tsx`:

- The unread indicator is an 8px `<span className="absolute ... bg-primary rounded-full" />` with no text, and the button's `aria-label` is a constant `"Notifications"`. Screen-reader users are never told there are unread items. The count is only visible inside the panel (`{unreadCount} new`).
- The button has `aria-expanded` but no `aria-haspopup` / `aria-controls`, and the panel is a plain `div` (focus-trapped through `useFocusTrap`) with no `role="dialog"` and no accessible name, so opening it announces nothing.
- The panel's list is a stack of `div`s rather than a list, and a notification's `read` state is conveyed only by colour and background.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The button label includes the count, for example "Notifications, 3 unread" (keep the plain label when 0), and the dot is `aria-hidden`
- [ ] The panel has `role="dialog"` (or a labelled `region`) with `aria-label="Notifications"`, and the button uses `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-controls`
- [ ] Notification items are `<ul>/<li>` and unread items contain visually-hidden "Unread" text
- [ ] Add or extend `NotificationBell` tests to assert the label and roles

## Tech Stack
Next.js, `apps/web/components/shared/NotificationBell.tsx`

## Notes
Distinct from the preference-toggle labelling issue on the profile page; this is the bell in the navbar.

title: Aria labels for breadcrumbs and page subnavigation
body:
We are overriding the `view/omeka/site/page/show.phtml` template for our sites to add ARIA labels to the breadcrumb `<nav>` and sub-menu `<nav>`. This is an accessibility best practice rather than a requirement, but I thought I would suggest adding it to Omeka S' base code, since it's such a simple addition.

We haven't gotten too fancy with the labels; just `<nav class="breadcrumb" aria-label="Breadcrumbs">` and `<nav class="sub-menu" aria-label="Pages in this section">`. It improves the screen reader experience, though, since it's clearer to the user what the distinct purposes of the multiple `<nav>`s are.

JumpLinks

**Describe the feature**
Follow up to comments in https://github.com/patternfly/patternfly-org/pull/3808

Basically right now the default value of the `aria-label` on JumpLinks is set to the `label` prop if passed in, and only if `label` is a string. Ideally we should consider making updates so that:

- an `aria-labelledby` prop can be passed in which can be given an `id` of the `label` element or some other element that labels the jump links nav. 

- if `label` is not a string and `aria-labelledby` is not manually passed in, generate a random `id` internally that's applied to the `label` wrapper element (pf-v5-c-jump-links__label), with that `id` passed to an aria-labelledby attribute on the outer JumpLinks `nav` element. 

- We could also consider removing the default value of the `aria-label` prop, but that may need to wait for a breaking change. Rationale here is that it would make more sense to link to the visible text label via `aria-labelledby` rather than repeat the text in an `aria-label`; while React is automating that for the consumer, it's only when the label prop is a string and in the HTML implementation there isn't that same automation provided by us

We should also add in a console warning if neither `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` are passed in, otherwise there's a chance that the JumpLinks internal `nav` has no proper accessible name.

**Are there visuals for this feature? If applicable, please include examples for each state and for varying widths**
Include screenshots or links to Marvel or other mockups.

**Any other information?**
A followup will need to be made in org to add verbiage to the a11y docs for JumpLinks

title: [dialog] Implement HasAriaDescription and HasAriaLabel interfaces
body:
### Motivation

Requested in https://github.com/vaadin/web-components/issues/473#issuecomment-5980781416

The new `HasAriaDescription` interface was added in Vaadin 25.3: https://github.com/vaadin/flow/pull/25117

It's added to field components, but is also relevant for `Dialog` to simplify setting ARIA attributes.

### Proposed Solution

Make `Dialog` implement both `HasAriaLabel` and `HasAriaDescription` interfaces to set attributes:

- `aria-label` + `aria-labelledby`
- `aria-description` + `aria-describedby` 

All of these should be set on `vaadin-dialog` itself, which uses `role="dialog"` - no overrides needed.

title: aria-labelled by for LabeledField
Accessibility point valueDecimals ignores zero
body:
### Expected behaviour

An explicit `accessibility.point.valueDecimals: 0` should format point descriptions as integers and override tooltip/chart precision.

### Actual behaviour

Accessibility number formatting uses truthy `||` fallbacks. The valid zero value is discarded, so a tooltip `valueDecimals: 2` can make the point ARIA label retain `1.23` despite the explicit accessibility override.

### Live demo with steps to reproduce

1. Configure `accessibility.point.valueDecimals` as `0`.
2. Configure `tooltip.valueDecimals` as `2`.
3. Add a point with value `1.23`.
4. Inspect its graphic `aria-label`; it retains `1.23` on current master.

### Product version

Current `master` (`c4e993d6`).

### Affected browser(s)

All.

title: Unterschiedliche Tooltip- und aria-label-Texte für bessere Barrierefreiheit ermöglichen
body:
### Ziele

Ermögliche das Setzen unterschiedlicher Texte für Tooltips und aria-labels, um den Anforderungen an Barrierefreiheit (Accessibility) gerecht zu werden – insbesondere für Anwendungsfälle, in denen zusätzliche Kontexte für Screenreader benötigt werden, die für sehende Nutzer im Tooltip nicht relevant sind.

### Hintergrund

Aktuell müssen für interaktive Elemente wie Filter-Badges Tooltip und aria-label identisch sein. In Barrierefreiheits-Prüfungen (z. B. BITV) wurde festgestellt, dass aria-labels spezifischen Kontext (wie den Namen des Filters) enthalten sollten, um die Verständlichkeit für Screenreader-Nutzer zu verbessern. Würde man diese Informationen jedoch auch im Tooltip anzeigen, würde dieser unnötig lang werden und die Nutzerfreundlichkeit für Sehende beeinträchtigen.

**Beispiel aktueller Zustand:**

[image]

In einer BITV-Prüfung kam der Hinweis:  
_"Filter Entfernen" sollte den entsprechenden Filter im zugänglichen Namen enthalten zur besseren Unterscheidbarkeit._

### Vorschlag

Führe eine Möglichkeit ein, unterschiedliche Texte für Tooltip und aria-label festzulegen. So könnte im aria-label auch der entsprechende Filtername gesetzt werden.

**Mockup gewünschtes Verhalten:**

[image]

---

**Bitte gib folgende zusätzliche Informationen an:**
- Für welche weiteren Komponenten oder UI-Elemente (außer Filter-Badges) wäre dieses Feature hilfreich?
- Sollen bestimmte Accessibility-Richtlinien oder Standards (z. B. WCAG, BITV) explizit berücksichtigt werden?
- Soll die Lösung dynamische Aktualisierungen beider Texte nach dem Rendern unterstützen?
- Gibt es technische Einschränkungen oder Präferenzen (z. B. beim API-Design), die beachtet werden sollten?

title: Feature: Show Captions in Audio Players
body:
## Context

`audioFeatures` has no text-track feature, and `<audio>` has no native cue rendering, so audio players can't show captions or transcripts. Vidstack's audio layout rendered captions in a text box. This matters for podcasts and accessibility.

## Acceptance criteria

- An audio preset can show caption or subtitle cues from a `<track>`.
- The audio skins include a captions control when tracks exist.
- The accessibility guide covers captions in audio players.

title: Feature: Render Captions in the Player
body:
## Context

Video.js 10 leaves caption rendering to the browser and asks you to style it with `::cue`. Vidstack rendered cues itself (`<media-captions>`), which gave it consistent positioning and styling across browsers, `data-part` hooks for voices, regions, and timed text, and captions for audio players.

Native rendering limits what the skins can do:

- In Firefox, captions aren't lifted above the controls (#2639).
- Caption style settings (#1437) depend on how much `::cue` exposes.
- `<audio>` has no native cue rendering.

## Acceptance criteria

- The player can render caption and subtitle cues in its own DOM, positioned relative to the controls in every supported browser.
- Rendered cues can be styled with documented hooks.
- Native rendering stays available where it's required, for example iPhone native fullscreen.

Related: #1437, #2639.

title: Feature: Caption Styling Customization
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Rough story-point estimate** from an AI-assisted planning pass — re-estimate when you pick this up.

User-adjustable caption appearance — font family, size, color, opacity, background, edge style, window — with preferences persisted to localStorage so they carry across sessions. An accessibility and UX expectation for long-form content; surfaced as a settings dialog in Video.js v8 and as granular props in Vidstack.

## Legal context

The FCC's [Closed Captioning Display Settings rule](https://www.fcc.gov/consumer-governmental-affairs/commission-announces-effective-date-closed-captioning-display-settings-rule) (under the [CVAA](https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/21st-century-communications-and-video-accessibility-act-cvaa)) requires covered entities to let viewers control caption appearance — font, size, color, opacity, edge style, background. Our [accessibility guide](https://videojs.org/docs/framework/html/concepts/accessibility#captions-and-subtitles) flags this too.

OS-level preferences would ideally flow through automatically, but there's no Web API yet — the [WebKit Caption Display Settings explainer](https://github.com/WebKit/explainers/tree/main/CaptionDisplaySettings) tracks the effort, with privacy/security concerns currently blocking standardization. Browsers are starting to ship their own UIs (Safari 26.4 added a [caption style profile menu](https://webkit.org/blog/17862/webkit-features-for-safari-26-4/)), but coverage is uneven, so we'll need to provide controls ourselves.

We already decided to render captions natively by default ([internal decision doc](https://github.com/videojs/v10/blob/main/internal/decisions/captions.md)). That means this feature either lives inside what native rendering allows (`::cue`, WebKit pseudo-selectors) or rides on the opt-in custom HTML overlay path the decision doc leaves open.

## Prior art

- **Video.js v8** — Full caption settings dialog (font family, color, opacity, background, window, edge style) persisted under `vjs-text-track-settings`. [TextTrackSettings source](https://github.com/videojs/video.js/blob/main/src/js/tracks/text-track-settings.js) · [text-tracks guide](https://videojs.com/guides/text-tracks/)
- **Vidstack** — Font menu with sliders and color pickers; each setting persists to `vds-player:${key}` in localStorage. [font-options.ts](https://github.com/vidstack/player/blob/main/packages/vidstack/src/core/font/font-options.ts) · [font-menu.ts](https://github.com/vidstack/player/blob/main/packages/vidstack/src/elements/define/layouts/default/ui/menu/font-menu.ts)
- **Mux Player** — No styling UI, but good prior art for what native rendering allows: `::cue` + `::-webkit-media-text-track-display` with CSS custom properties to scale captions with the player. [gerwig theme](https://github.com/muxinc/elements/blob/main/packages/mux-player/src/themes/gerwig/gerwig.html) · [custom-media-element](https://github.com/muxinc/media-elements/blob/main/packages/custom-media-element/custom-media-element.ts) · [styling guide](https://www.mux.com/docs/guides/player-customize-look-and-feel)
- **Media Chrome** — Exposes a track picker but no styling UI; delegates to the host theme. [media-captions-menu-button](https://github.com/muxinc/media-chrome/blob/main/src/js/menu/media-captions-menu-button.ts)
- **Plyr** — No styling UI. Active user requests: [#1215](https://github.com/sampotts/plyr/issues/1215), [#1893](https://github.com/sampotts/plyr/issues/1893)

## Related

- Customer request for Mux Player (e.g. Typeform)
- Internal discussion in #project-vjs10 (2026-02-24) that led to the native-rendering decision

title: Bug: Shift Native Captions Above Controls in Firefox
body:
## Description

Tested with `@videojs/html` `10.0.0-beta.25`.

The default video skin sets `--media-caption-track-y` when controls are visible, but applies that offset only through `video::-webkit-media-text-track-container`. Firefox does not support this WebKit-only pseudo-element, so native WebVTT captions overlap the visible control bar.

This behavior originates from / is contextualized by #636, which introduced native caption shifting for video skins.

## Reproduction

1. Render the default `<video-skin>` with a native `<track>` containing WebVTT captions.
2. Open it in Firefox and enable captions.
3. Hover the video to reveal the controls.
4. Observe that captions overlap the visible control bar.

## Expected behavior

Native captions should shift upward and clear the controls while the control bar is visible in Firefox.

title: Bug: Default Skin Hides the Captions Button on Players Narrower Than 32rem
body:
## Context

The default skin hides its captions button on players narrower than the `lg` container size (32rem). The neutral skin (formerly minimal, renamed in #3092) hides it below `xs`. Both rules come from the shared styles in `packages/skins/src/styles/layout/controls.styles.ts`:

```ts
captionsButton: { default: 'media-max-lg:hidden', neutral: 'media-max-xs:hidden' }
```

The registry skin source carries the same class, so on phones captions are reachable only through the settings menu. In the rc.4 agent-eval validation (#2893), the `customize-source-skin-mobile` task asked agents to keep captions next to volume on phones. All 12 attempts removed this class to make the button show.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide whether the captions toggle should stay visible on narrow players in the default skin. It's an accessibility-relevant control, and the neutral skin already keeps it visible down to a smaller size.
- Whatever is decided is documented in the skin customization docs, including how to change it in the skin source.

Let authors add their own captions for embedded videos that do not have complete or adequate captions.

### Problem Description
When authors embed videos that are not WCAG compliant due to captioning issues (missing, auto-generated, or inaccurate), there is currently no way for them to provide visitors an alternative set of captions.

### Affected Users
Authors who embed videos and readers who use assistive technology.

### Importance and Impact
WCAG compliance; if this option is not available, authors would have to remove or replace videos.
Specifically requested by a network manager ([link](https://pressbooks.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/26251) for internal use only).

### Proposed Solution
Offer a alternative media player like [Able Player](https://wordpress.org/plugins/ableplayer) 

### Current Workaround

title: Create slot for summary fig caption in charts

title: Adding an Accessibility Tips page
body:
## Feature Request

**Is your feature request related to a problem or unsupported use case? Please describe.**
This Accessibility Tips page could help reassure users about the accessibility features offered by Visio.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A page with a list of the features offered, a list of shortcuts set up to access meeting functions (keyboard shortcuts, transcription, recording, etc.), as well as how to access the meeting using the browser's native modals.

And this page would be accessible right from the start, even before logging into the application, to be transparent with users with disabilities.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
This page must be in HTML format and not created on a content management platform, which could potentially be more difficult to access with keyboard navigation, for example. I'm thinking particularly of the support section.

title: Cadrer la carte sur la France entière et faire ressortir les massifs du 13
body:
## Objectif
Recadrer la carte interactive (et son repli statique sans JavaScript) sur la France entière avec un
fond neutre et pâle, en faisant nettement ressortir les massifs des Bouches-du-Rhône — remplissage plus
foncé et contours plus marqués — afin qu'un décideur communal identifie immédiatement le territoire
couvert au sein du territoire national. Demande du propriétaire du projet.

## Lignes de la DoD servies
- §12 — la carte interactive affiche le fond OpenStreetMap auto-hébergé et les massifs colorés selon
  leur statut (élargit le cadrage sans rouvrir cette exigence).
- §12 — le repli image statique sans JavaScript reste l'équivalent fonctionnel de la carte (contrat #9) :
  son cadrage doit rester identique à celui de la carte interactive.
- §12 — accessibilité AA bloquante : aucune information n'est portée par la seule couleur, contrastes
  vérifiés à 200 % de zoom et 360 px sans scroll horizontal.

## Contexte et contrainte n°2 (zéro requête vers un domaine tiers)
Le cadrage actuel est resserré sur les Bouches-du-Rhône. Étendre la vue à la France entière suppose
d'héberger nous-mêmes les tuiles correspondantes : c'est seulement tenable en **pyramide asymétrique**,
sur le modèle de ce que `massifs_fond_de_carte()` expose déjà (`zoom_min` / `zoom_max`) :
- France entière aux zooms bas uniquement (ordre de grandeur z5–z8),
- Bouches-du-Rhône seul aux zooms hauts (z9 et au-delà, cadrage actuel inchangé).

Avant toute ingestion, **chiffrer le volume de tuiles et le poids disque** de la pyramide France z5–z8 et
documenter le résultat dans le corps de la chaîne (commentaire ou contrat). Aucune tuile, à aucun zoom,
n'est servie depuis un domaine tiers.

## Tâches
- [ ] Chiffrer le nombre de tuiles et le poids disque de la pyramide France entière aux zooms bas
      (z5–z8) avant toute ingestion ; consigner le résultat.
- [ ] Étendre la génération des tuiles (`includes/ingest/tuiles/build/`) à une source France entière
      pour les zooms bas, en conservant la source Bouches-du-Rhône aux zooms hauts (pyramide asymétrique,
      jamais de recouvrement de domaine tiers).
- [ ] Adapter `massifs_fond_de_carte()` et ses métadonnées pour exposer la pyramide asymétrique
      (bornes de zoom par échelle) sans casser le contrat existant consommé par `carte.php`.
- [ ] Élargir le cadrage initial et les bornes (`maxBounds`/`bbox`) de `assets/js/carte/carte.js` à la
      France entière, tout en gardant le zoom élevé centré sur les Bouches-du-Rhône par défaut.
- [ ] Ajouter la mise en valeur visuelle des massifs du 13 dans `assets/css/carte.css`, à partir de
      jetons dédiés de `design-system/MASTER.md` (fond atténué + remplissage/contour foncés), sans
      valeur brute posée en CSS ou en JS.
- [ ] Porter l'information de mise en valeur par un second canal que la couleur seule (contour renforcé,
      motif ou libellé), conformément à l'AA bloquante.
- [ ] Régénérer `assets/img/carte-statique.png` (repli sans JavaScript) avec le même cadrage France et
      la même mise en valeur des massifs du 13 que la carte interactive.
- [ ] Vérifier les contrastes du fond atténué et des polygones à 200 % de zoom et à 360 px.

## Empreinte fichiers
- `wp-content/plugins/massifs-core/includes/ingest/tuiles/fond.php`
- `wp-content/plugins/massifs-core/includes/ingest/tuiles/metadonnees.php`
- `wp-content/plugins/massifs-core/includes/ingest/tuiles/module.php`
- `wp-content/plugins/massifs-core/includes/ingest/tuiles/build/` (config source + script de génération)
- `wp-content/plugins/massifs-core/data/tuiles/` (nouvel artefact France, zooms bas)
- `wp-content/themes/massifs/assets/js/carte/carte.js`
- `wp-content/themes/massifs/assets/css/carte.css`
- `wp-content/themes/massifs/assets/css/tokens.css` (nouveaux jetons de fond atténué / mise en valeur)
- `wp-content/themes/massifs/assets/img/carte-statique.png`
- `wp-content/themes/massifs/templates/parts/carte.php` (si l'îlot JSON doit porter la pyramide asymétrique)

## Contraintes applicables

title: UI-25: Disclosure: destination is a switch, and class colours read as warnings
body:
**Status:** Ready — Pass E spec linked below (https://github.com/qwts/overlook/issues/1310#issuecomment-5882474959).

**Severity:** P2 · **Pass:** E — Selection pill, Review Duplicates, Export · **Owner:** Design first
**Parent:** #1310

### Evidence
`DisclosurePreview.tsx` uses a Switch for “Publishing to a public destination”. TONES maps Private to amber and Public to red. Widening uses an unstyled native `<input type=checkbox>`.

### Cause
Private is the safe default, but amber marks it as a caution. Red for Public reads as an error, and the native checkbox ignores the theme.

### Resolution
Destination is a Segmented control (Named recipient · Public). Badges are neutral with icons, and widening uses the shared Checkbox.

Spec: https://github.com/qwts/overlook/issues/1310#issuecomment-5882474959

### Done when
- [ ] The surface matches the Pass E spec in the design system (dark, light, high contrast)
- [ ] Keyboard, focus, and screen-reader behavior are unchanged or better; checked with axe and at 200% zoom
- [ ] Storybook story updated to show the fixed state

### References
- Design-system audit: `UI Audit 2026-09.html` §08
- Accessibility contract: design system `guidelines/accessibility.md`
- Tokens of record: `src/renderer/src/styles/tokens/`
- Related: #1139 (collection/photo disclosure override UI reuses the same disclosure rows)

title: Slider announcement does not reflect selected range or updated values
body:
When the sliders are adjusted, an announcement is made similar to the behavior of the Zoom controls. However, the same announcement is read regardless of the slider positions, so it does not accurately reflect the user’s selected range.

In addition, there is no immediate feedback indicating what each slider has been set to. The only way to determine the updated value is to navigate away from the slider and then back to it, at which point the percentage value has changed. Even then, the percentage alone is not especially helpful context.

#### Expected behaviour
The announcement should accurately reflect the selected range after the slider is adjusted.
If the range announcement is accurate and complete, there is no need to separately announce the position of the individual slider.
Users should receive clear and immediate feedback when adjusting the slider.

#### Actual behaviour
Adjusting a slider triggers an announcement.
The announcement does not change based on the slider’s position.
Users do not receive immediate feedback about the selected value or range.
Updated values are only apparent after moving focus away and back to the slider.

title: A11y: Outline and apply texture to property polygons in the map
body:
## Description
The properties shown in the map are hard to distinguish and differentiate; boundaries are unclear and the priority is only conveyed through color alone. To make it visually accessible, we should outline and apply texture on the property polygons.

## Potential Solutions
- Apply 1.5-2px outline on property polygon (black or near black color #313537)
- Apply texture fill as an additional indicator for priority
  <details>
  <summary> Sample screenshot when properties are outlined </summary>

  [image]

  </details>

## For Considerations
At high zoom (out) levels, the outline and the pattern applied to the polygons can drastically diminish the color coding, making the experience more ambiguous and counter-intuitive. We should explore:

- Only outline polygons at lower zoom levels
  - Identify the minimum zoom level when we start to show the outlined polygons
- Only fill the polygons with texture at lower zoom levels
  - Identify the minimum zoom level when we start to show the texture

We should explore, test & iterate on this idea.

title: Widen LITERAL_SCAN_ROOTS to every new frontend area and add an accessibility gate to the pull-request gate set
body:
**Why.** The plan adds pairing, invite, recovery, storage, and quota interfaces and never mentions accessibility or internationalization, in a repository that enforces both in CI. The hole is mechanical and currently open: `LITERAL_SCAN_ROOTS` at scripts/check-ui-i18n.mjs:67 is `Object.freeze(['ui/src/App.tsx', 'ui/src/components'])`, while the change map places new user-facing copy at `ui/src/pairing/`, `ui/src/invites/`, `ui/src/storage/`, `ui/src/runtime/`, and `ui/src/sw.ts` (docs/production-deployment.md:838-842) — all outside the scan. Copy written there ships untranslated with green CI. The plan's own twelve new pull-request gates (docs/production-deployment.md:649-667) include neither an accessibility nor an internationalization gate, and pairing is the new onboarding, where a pointer-only, sighted-only assumption is easiest to make: SAS strings, QR codes, and recovery phrases are specified with no non-visual alternative. Without this, the first production surface regresses the EN/FR parity and keyboard operability the repository already holds elsewhere, and the regression is invisible to CI.

**Source.** docs/production-deployment-decision.md:161-176 (A5, "Blocks: the Phase 2 gate"); current `LITERAL_SCAN_ROOTS` value at scripts/check-ui-i18n.mjs:67 and `EXEMPT_FILES` at scripts/check-ui-i18n.mjs:73-91; new frontend areas in the repository change map at docs/production-deployment.md:846-850; pull-request gate set at docs/production-deployment.md:650-667; Phase 2 go/no-go gate at docs/production-deployment.md:939-948; review findings F3, F6, F30

**Acceptance criteria.**

- [ ] `LITERAL_SCAN_ROOTS` at scripts/check-ui-i18n.mjs:67 is widened from `['ui/src/App.tsx', 'ui/src/components']` to cover each new frontend area named in the change map at docs/production-deployment.md:846-850 — `ui/src/sw.ts`, `ui/src/runtime/`, `ui/src/storage/`, `ui/src/pairing/`, `ui/src/invites/` — "in the same change that creates it" (A5, decision line 173-174), not afterwards
- [ ] Widening the scan does not silently sweep in the `EXEMPT_FILES` entries at scripts/check-ui-i18n.mjs:76 onward, per the standing note at lines 73-75; each entry remains listed with its recorded reason, and rule 5's stale side still reports an exemption whose file is gone
- [ ] Every new user-visible surface enters `ui/src/l10n/catalog.ts` in both `en.ts` and `fr.ts`, and check-ui-i18n.mjs passes on it — including rule 3 (no French value byte-identical to its English counterpart without a recorded, stale-checked exemption) and rule 4 (French typography, U+202F before the marks named in docs/glossary-fr.md decision 7)
- [ ] The pull-request gate list at docs/production-deployment.md:650-667 gains an accessibility gate and an internationalization gate alongside the existing "CSP and Trusted Types tests" bullet at line 664, and every new destination enters `ui/e2e/a11y-matrix.spec.ts` under its recorded contract: no critical/serious axe violations, all destinations x 4 viewports
- [ ] The pairing section specifies a manual-entry code path as the alternative to QR, and how the short authentication string is announced to a screen reader with character disambiguation
- [ ] An explicit decision, with its reason per docs/i18n.md rule 1, records whether the recovery-phrase wordlist is translated or is a never-translate token
- [ ] The Phase 2 go/no-go gate at docs/production-deployment.md:939-948 carries an item that does not pass while any new user-facing surface sits outside `LITERAL_SCAN_ROOTS`, outside the EN/FR catalogs, or outside `ui/e2e/a11y-matrix.spec.ts`

**Blocked by.** nothing

title: Consider ways to allow a user to permanently suppress the low resolution error
body:
### User Experience

### Current User Experience
Sometimes, a user must knowingly run Foundry VTT with resolution that repeatedly triggers the "Low Resolution" error:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3605541/229001163-89b40c59-5d5d-4956-916c-2020084046cd.png

This can happen due to hardware limitations, and also due to accessibility issues. For users who this affect, this can be quite disruptive. For example, this was originally opened by #9144, before that issue was repurposed for a different fix. This is another example from a customer support email:

> As someone with low vision, I run my desktop at a lower than typical screen resolution (1080p 19x10), and have font scaling at 150% which makes the effective resolution even lower.[...]
> 
> Currently, Foundry (and in Forge) throws a red "...requires a usable window dimensions..." error which requires a click to dismiss, as if it were a critical failure. And it's not in one place, it's actually in mulitple places. Foundry start, world load, in-game when you change browser zoom levels.  and other triggers as well. THIS IS VERY ANNOYING. 
### Existing workarounds
Some modules have cropped up that help address this, notably https://foundryvtt.com/packages/custom-css, https://foundryvtt.com/packages/hide-player-ui, and https://foundryvtt.com/packages/warning-remove but none are currently updated for V14.
### Proposed solution
Create a new client-level core setting that converts this error to a console-only log statement

title: [🧪 a11y] Ensure WCAG 2.2 AA Compliance Across Oxygen UI
body:
Since you already have **Storybook**, I'd make the issue more actionable by including accessibility testing in Storybook rather than just mentioning `axe-core`.

---

### Current Limitation

`@wso2/oxygen-ui` is built on top of Material UI (MUI), which provides strong accessibility support out of the box. However, Oxygen UI customizes and extends many of these components through wrappers, custom styling, composition, and additional functionality.

These customizations may unintentionally introduce accessibility regressions or deviate from **WCAG 2.1 AA** requirements. Additionally, accessibility is not currently validated as part of the Storybook development workflow.

### Suggested Improvement

Conduct a comprehensive accessibility audit of all Oxygen UI components to ensure that our wrappers and custom components preserve the accessibility guarantees provided by MUI and remain compliant with **WCAG 2.1 AA**.

The audit should verify:

* Keyboard navigation and focus management
* Visible focus indicators
* Correct semantic HTML and ARIA attributes
* Screen reader compatibility
* Accessible naming for controls and icons
* Color contrast compliance
* Forms, validation, and error announcements
* Accessibility of dialogs, menus, popovers, tooltips, tabs, accordions, and other interactive components
* Responsiveness and support for zoom/reflow
* Support for `prefers-reduced-motion`
* No accessibility regressions introduced through custom wrappers, theming, or styling

As part of this effort, integrate accessibility checks into Storybook (e.g., using the Storybook Accessibility addon powered by `axe-core`) so that accessibility issues can be identified during component development and review.

### Acceptance Criteria

* Audit all public Oxygen UI components against **WCAG 2.1 AA**.
* Verify that wrapper components preserve MUI's accessibility behavior.
* Integrate accessibility testing into Storybook.
* Ensure all component stories pass accessibility checks or document known exceptions.
* Identify and document accessibility issues or regressions.
* Create follow-up issues for components requiring significant remediation.
* Resolve high-priority accessibility issues.
* Document accessibility considerations and usage guidelines for component consumers.

### References

* WCAG 2.1: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG21/)
* Storybook Accessibility: [https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/accessibility](https://storybook.js.org/docs/essentials/accessibility)
* Material UI Accessibility: [https://mui.com/material-ui/guides/accessibility/](https://mui.com/material-ui/guides/accessibility/)
* WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: [https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)

This makes the issue not just an audit, but also establishes an ongoing accessibility workflow within Storybook to help prevent regressions.

title: Heatmap a11y issues
body:
### In all locations 1. The map itself gets keyboard focus, but has no label or focus outline, so it's a mystery stop. - [x] add a focus outline to the same div that has `tabindex=”0”` - [x] add `aria-label=”heatmap”` to the same div - identification will also be helped by exposed its `
`, see #1787 ### In search results 2. Keyboard gets to the list of titles, but the sidebar doesn’t open on keyboard focus - only when you click into the map. If you have SR on, you can hear the list of titles, but if you are just a keyboard user - you get a bunch of tabstops with no apparent content. (Gif at the bottom shows me tabbing through the titles. You can see the URL at the bottom left change, but no other indication that anything is changing.) - [ ] open the sidebar when any item in it has keyboard focus 3. The keyboard can get to the zoom in/out buttons, but cannot pan the map. If Zoom takes the highlighted area outside the frame, too bad. I don’t know how to solve this one. Does leaflet has some kind of key combination pan feature? 4. For all users, there’s no pagination past the first 50 results. No way to close the side panel once it’s open. Frequently, the panel pushes the selected square out of view when it opens, changing or zeroing out the list of results. This feature in general has usability issues. ### Individual result page 5. Marker is in the tab order, but has no action or information associated with it. Is it interactive in some contexts? - The marker img is missing alt text, and is perceivable, so: - [ ] add `alt=“location marker”` 6. Outline is not in tab order. AMP reports it as an svg without a title, but it doesn’t seem to be perceived by the SR so I’m leaving it as is. ------- **Tabbing without visual indicator (watch bottom left corner).** [image]

title: Accessibilité : WCAG AA et navigation clavier sur la version bureau
body:
## Contexte
§6 : « Contrastes conformes WCAG AA, navigation clavier sur la version bureau ».

## Périmètre
- [ ] Contrastes AA vérifiés sur les deux thèmes, y compris sur les graphiques (§4.7)
- [ ] **Navigation clavier complète sur la version bureau** : saisie d'une volée entièrement au clavier, tabulation ordonnée, focus visible
- [ ] Rôles et libellés ARIA sur les composants de saisie
- [ ] Annonces des changements d'état (nouveau joueur actif, bust, fin de leg) aux lecteurs d'écran
- [ ] L'information n'est jamais portée par la seule couleur
- [ ] Respect de `prefers-reduced-motion`
- [ ] Audit automatisé (axe) intégré à la CI

## Critères d'acceptation
- Un leg complet se joue au clavier seul sur la version bureau
- L'audit automatisé ne remonte aucune violation critique
- Les zones de tap font au minimum 48 × 48 px partout (§5)

## Référence CDC
§4.7, §5, §6

title: Automated WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA accessibility testing in CI
body: The README claims WCAG 2.1 AA but no axe/pa11y/Lighthouse check enforces it. Danish public-sector services (EN 301 549) require structured accessibility testing. Add axe integration to the Playwright suite plus a pa11y/Lighthouse baseline, failing CI on Level AA violations.

title: Perform an a11y/WCAG review
body:
Thanks for creating an issue! Please fill out this form so we can be sure to have all the information we need, and to minimize back and forth.

* **What are we trying to do?**

We've got a decent userbase and haven't holistically looked at accessibility for our case management corps. Disability and accommodation are a reproductive justice issue so we should take the time to step back and make sure our software matches our values on this.

* **What feature or behavior is this required for?**

Making sure anyone who wants to case manage can do so without fighting with our system.

* **How could we solve this issue? (Not knowing is okay!)**

We should use this ticket to go thru the a11y and WCAG lists and see what they recommend doing, what linters we can set up, etc. I suspect there are easy wins to be had.

* **Anything else?**

Hold on implementing or breaking tickets out until the case management team has had a chance to add an accessibility question to their own case management materials.
